hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split ID/EX sequential updates into a narrow control/valid group and
a payload group. On a flush, clear the entire ctrl field and valid
exactly as the existing zero bundle does. Do not clear, mask, or hold
payload registers merely because of flush. Keep their deterministic
reset-to-zero behavior, but otherwise capture pc, predicted_next_pc,
both operand values, immediate, register addresses, rd, and instruction
whenever there is no actual backend hold. Each field must have exactly
one sequential driver; do not mix whole-struct and partial assignments
across separate always_ff blocks.

Make stall_id mean only dmem_stall || div_wait. Remove load_use_hazard
from this ID/EX hold signal while preserving stall_if, flush_if,
flush_id, stall_ex_mem, and hold_mem_wb behavior. This is a redundant
hold removal: whenever a load-use hazard occurs without a backend
hold, the existing flush_id already forces an ID/EX bubble. On that
edge the payload may capture the still-unaccepted younger instruction,
but ctrl=0 and valid=0 make it inert, and the held fetch is accepted
normally on the following eligible edge. When a memory or divide wait
is active, both control and payload must remain held exactly as before.
Preserve reset priority and flush priority for the control/valid group.

Clearing valid alone is insufficient: forwarding and memory control
logic consult ctrl fields even when valid is zero. Continue clearing
all control bits on every flush, particularly reg_write, mem_read,
mem_write, is_branch, and is_jump. Retained or newly captured bubble
payload must never launch a divide, redirect, train the predictor,
forward as a writer, access memory, or retire. Leave EX/MEM full-bundle
divide bubbles and MEM/WB forwarding-data retention unchanged. All
live instructions retain their exact operands, instruction metadata,
accepted prediction, trap behavior, and RVFI fields through holds.

This single micro-optimization removes recovery and load-use logic
from the wide payload registers' direct reset and enable controls.
Existing upstream instruction-to-NOP selection may still affect data
inputs; it need not be redesigned. Add no stage, state bit, execution
shortcut, new prediction behavior, or architectural latency. Preserve
nret=1, all external ports, all decoder legality rules, and every hard
invariant and evaluation check.

Expect an unmeasured three-percent fitness improvement from higher
median Fmax, with identical bracketed cycles for the same binary and
bus-ready schedule. Confidence is medium: the other winning seeds are
limited by local predictor tag-to-counter-enable paths at 6.36 and
6.42 ns, so they may cap the benefit; synthesis may also reconstruct
unwanted control dependencies or alter placement adversely. Inspect
the mapped payload reset/enable cones and routed critical paths to
establish whether the intended control isolation survives synthesis.

Run the existing unit, formal, stalled cosim, and three-seed FPGA gates.
Compare accepted bus transactions and valid RVFI retirements, including
their cycle positions, against the current winner under identical
inputs; inactive payload bit patterns need not match. Use full-precision
iterations/bracketed-cycles times median Fmax and report LUT/FF costs.
The saved 371.55 result is documented as a 2 KB scored run; the separate
canonical 6 KB winner run takes 30,822,790 bracketed cycles. Keep those
configurations distinct and unchanged, and verify the required 6 KB
CRCs d4b0/be52/5e47, memory bounds, markers, and validation UART literal.

title: Separate ID/EX validity from the wide recovery payload
motivation:
The current ID/EX register clears its entire packed bundle on reset OR
flush. In addition, IF replaces the entire instruction with a NOP on
recovery, putting redirect into instruction decode, register addressing,
and load-hazard inputs. Thus a one-instruction squash controls hundreds
of payload bits even though only the instruction's validity must change.

The structural history identifies this as a recurring timing limit.
hyp-20260905-002-r3s1 removed indexed predictor maintenance from the
critical paths but exposed hazard/divide control into ID/EX resets.
The current winner, hyp-20260905-002-r4s1, reports 156.62 MHz median
Fmax and 371.55 fitness. Its median seed has a 6.39 ns path from
predicted_next_pc[0] through mismatch/hazard control to an ID/EX
operand register's RESET pin. The other two seeds remain limited by
local predictor comparisons. Earlier store buffering saved only 0.75%
of cycles, and the divider split saved area without timed-cycle gains.
Separating instruction validity from payload transport directly attacks
the measured recovery fanout while retaining the current schedule.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the IF-to-ID/EX boundary around a separate registered valid
token. Keep the current pipeline depth, single issue, exact accepted
prediction metadata, and one-younger-slot recovery. This experiment
changes squash distribution, with no predictor-policy, arithmetic,
memory-latency, or instruction-scheduling redesign.

In IF, always present raw imem_data as out.instr. Keep out.valid low
on flush or redirect, and preserve the existing PC update priorities:
reset, immediate EX redirect, then accepted predicted advancement.
Recovery must still override instruction-bus backpressure. Preserve
every predictor table, pending event, training rule, and commit edge.
Removing the recovery-controlled NOP mux is necessary; splitting only
the ID/EX register would leave a second wide recovery-to-payload path.

In ID, register validity separately from the decoded control and wide
payload. The valid register retains the existing reset/flush priority
over capture/hold: reset or flush clears it, otherwise !stall captures
in.valid, otherwise it holds. Payload registers capture the raw PC,
prediction, instruction, immediate, register addresses, operand values,
and decoded control whenever !stall, even when flush is asserted.
Their existing reset initialization can remain. Flush must not select
their reset, data mux, or clock enable. In particular, do not replace
the old wide flush reset with a wide flush-controlled hold enable.
Keep the public id_ex_t layout and module ports unchanged.

At the ID/EX output boundary, expose the captured payload unchanged
but present ctrl='0 whenever the REGISTERED valid token is zero.
Valid instructions see their complete original decoded control.
This compact control mask reproduces the current downstream bubble
contract without zeroing operands, addresses, PCs, or instructions.
It is essential because hazard, forwarding, and memory logic currently
inspect control fields independently of retirement validity. Invalid
raw stores, loads, jumps, illegal instructions, and DIV/REM encodings
must not request memory, write registers, launch a divide, redirect,
train the predictor, or retire. Do not mask the entire packed bundle.
Decoder legality defaults and all valid-instruction trap rules remain
exactly as before.

Preserve hazard_unit's raw source-field comparison and stall equations.
With raw IF data, its load-use match must remain independent of
redirect, flush, and the combinational IF valid signal; qualifying
that match with recovery-derived validity would reconnect redirect
to the wide payload clock enable. A raw match on an unavailable fetch
or a killed fetch is harmless: imem backpressure already prevents
acceptance, redirect overrides the PC hold, and ID/EX validity clears.
A real load-use interlock still creates exactly one bubble. Memory
backpressure and divide waits still hold the active ID/EX payload and
valid token. Preserve EX/MEM drain behavior, accepted divide operands,
and MEM/WB's retained forwarding fields when only retirement validity
clears during a memory hold; do not gate that retained bypass by its
cleared retirement-valid bit.

Predict unchanged accepted-fetch, resolution, bus-handshake, and RVFI
retirement schedules for identical input streams, with higher Fmax
from lower recovery fanout. Estimate a three percent fitness gain;
it is unmeasured. The new valid-to-control mask can become critical,
and the near-equal local predictor paths in the other seeds may cap
the improvement. Inspect synthesized cones and all three routed seeds
to confirm that combinational redirect/flush no longer reaches ID/EX

title: Eight-entry return stack with direct return recognition
motivation:
The current predictor remembers one last destination per tagged PC. A
return shared by several callers therefore either predicts the previous
caller's continuation or misses after target-table eviction. The saved
6 KB CoreMark ELF has several call sites for crcu16 and crc16, providing
a concrete opportunity for caller-sensitive return prediction; this is
static evidence, not a measured return-misprediction rate.

Prior predictor experiments favor a small, simple lookup: r2s2's two-way
table lost Fmax without reducing cycles, and r4s2's shared bank commands
lost frequency through routing. Retain r4s1's 16-entry target table and
private registered training events. Add one focused predictor mechanism
that can eliminate return-recovery bubbles, including on target-table
misses, while keeping its top address directly in registers.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add an eight-entry return-address stack (RAS) to if_stage. Recognize only
the exact canonical return instructions JALR x0,x1,0 and JALR x0,x5,0
directly from raw imem_data. When either instruction is fetched and the
RAS is nonempty, predict its registered top address. Otherwise use the
existing tagged target prediction and PC+4 fallback unchanged. A RAS
prediction does not require a target-table hit. This narrow constant
instruction match introduces no register-file read or target adder in
IF. Use raw imem_data, never the flush-dependent out.instr, for the match.

Keep all eight full 32-bit return addresses in a shift stack, with entry
zero as the directly readable top and a four-bit occupancy count in
0..8. Compute return recognition and the existing target-table lookup in
parallel, and select among sequential PC, table target, and RAS top with
mutually exclusive source enables. Avoid an indexed stack read on the
fetch path. The stack is address-history prediction only: no additional
instruction stage, frontend interlock, or architectural stack is added.

Derive push/pop hints from the decoded instruction in EX, qualified by
the existing resolve_valid and resolve_legal, including misalignment
checks. Treat x1 and x5 as link registers. A legal JAL pushes PC+4 iff
rd is a link register. For a legal JALR: push when only rd is a link
register; pop when only rs1 is a link register; push when both are the
same link register; pop then push when both are different link registers;
otherwise do neither. These hints update history even for noncanonical
JALRs, but only the two exact zero-immediate return encodings above may
select the RAS in IF. All other JALRs retain last-target prediction.

Preserve the successful EX-to-predictor register boundary. At resolution
edge N capture just a pending action and, for pushes, the full PC+4 link
value. Commit the action on edge N+1 against the CURRENT stack while
accepting the next action. Do not snapshot the stack or feed live EX
operands, comparisons, or flags into stack commit logic. Reuse EX's
existing PC+4 value for link data. This supports one action per cycle
without maintenance forwarding. No speculative fetch-time push or pop,
checkpoint, rollback, or pending-action bypass is required.

Push shifts retained addresses down and installs the new link at the
top; occupancy saturates at eight and overflow discards the oldest
address. A nonempty pop shifts addresses up and decrements occupancy;
an empty pop is a no-op. Pop-then-push replaces the top at unchanged
nonzero occupancy, or installs one entry when empty. Reset clears
occupancy and pending validity with priority over capture and commit;
unused address payloads need not reset and must remain masked.

Refresh pending validity every non-reset edge. An accepted older action
commits once through subsequent fetch stalls, memory holds, divide waits,
and younger redirects. Such events may prevent new EX acceptance but
must not replay, hold, cancel, or duplicate an already accepted action.
Wrong-path calls never reach valid EX resolution. A mispredicted call
still pushes its correct architectural PC+4 when it resolves legally.

Fetch uses pre-edge committed RAS and target-table state. Neither bus
backpressure nor a load-use/divide hold consumes a prediction or pops
the stack. The added training delay can leave the stack stale for very
short callees or consecutive returns; accept the resulting prediction
misses and recover with the existing exact next-PC comparison. Preserve
the exact prediction captured with each accepted instruction, recovery
for EVERY advancing instruction, redirect priority over imem stalls,
and architectural next-PC reporting in RVFI. Incorrect hints, overwritten
link registers, overflow, and underflow must affect performance only.

Estimate a two-percent net fitness improvement, not a measured result.
The direct imem-to-next-PC recognition path, stack update fanout, and
roughly 300 added state bits may reduce Fmax; caller changes may also
be too rare to repay that cost. Measure the actual product of full-
precision iterations/cycle and three-seed median Fmax, with identical
ELFs, toolchain, and ready schedules for current RTL and candidate.
Report bracketed cycles, return-related recoveries, Fmax, LUT4/FF cost,
and critical-path endpoints. Use the unchanged correctness and FPGA
gates, including stalled execution, bounds, timing markers, and UART.
Validate the requested 6 KB run and canonical d4b0/be52/5e47 CRCs. The
historical log identifies 371.55 as the scored 2 KB result; report that
comparison separately from 6 KB throughput without changing either
evaluation contract. Keep nret=1, external IO, decoder legality, RVFI
order and traps, memory behavior, and all M-extension logic intact.

implementation_notes:
Implemented the eight-entry return-address stack in `cores/bench`. Correctness checks pass. The measured hypothesis does not improve fitness: the 6 KB throughput product decreases 3.963175%, and the separate scored 2 KB product decreases 3.981512%. The proposed +2% was an estimate, not a measured result.

Changes:

- `rtl/if_stage.sv`: eight full 32-bit shift-stack entries, directly readable entry-zero top, four-bit saturating occupancy, and a registered valid/push/pop/link event. Resolution edge N captures the event; edge N+1 commits against current history while accepting the next event. Push discards the oldest entry on overflow; empty pop does nothing; pop/push replaces a nonempty top or creates one entry. Reset clears occupancy and pending validity. Payloads remain unreset and masked.
- IF recognizes only raw `imem_data` values `0x00008067` and `0x00028067`. Mutually exclusive sequential/table/RAS enables select the next PC. RAS selection is independent of table residency. All 16 table rows, private registered training events, target memory, counters, transition rules, and commit timing remain intact.
- `rtl/ex_stage.sv`: decoded x1/x5 JAL/JALR hints are qualified by existing advancing resolution and legality, including target misalignment. The existing PC+4 expression is factored into one shared value for architectural link writes, sequential recovery, and pending RAS link data. Same-link JALRs push; different-link JALRs pop/push. Live EX signals terminate at the RAS event registers.
- `rtl/core.sv`: internal hint/link connections only. Core ports, nret=1, retirement order, exact accepted-prediction recovery, architectural RVFI next PC, decoder, hazards, memory, and M-extension logic are preserved.
- `test/test_if_stage.py`: independent public-output logical-stack reference with explicit delayed events, every occupancy, overflow/underflow, replacement at every depth, consecutive actions, all address bits, wrapped links, pre-edge visibility, raw decode despite flush, table hit/miss fallback, near encodings, reset cancellation, and once-only draining through holds/redirects. Existing table-policy/collision assertions are retained.
- `test/test_pipeline.py`: independent instruction-word hint classification and delayed logical history. Added alternating callers with deliberate return-table eviction, x1/x5 hint matrix, noncanonical and trapping JALRs, nested/tail/coroutine calls, eleven-level recursion, overwritten links, empty/short/consecutive returns, wrong-path calls/stores, memory-dependent held JALRs, instruction stalls, divide drain, reset before commit, and PC+4 wraparound. title: Replace local saturating-counter arithmetic with thermometer state
motivation:
The current winner reaches 388.66 fitness at 163.83 MHz after isolating
ID/EX payload controls. The bench history identifies another specific
timing opportunity: r4s1's seeds 1 and 3 ended at local predictor-counter
clock enables, reached from committed or pending tags in 6.36/6.42 ns.
Row-private event registers already isolate these updates from live EX.
However, each row still uses binary increment/decrement, saturation
selection, and conditional counter writes after its full-tag comparison.

Prior micro_opt attempts at register-file selection and ALU predecode
did not produce accepted gains, and r4s0's preserved equality tree lost
14.62 percent by exposing a different path. This hypothesis instead
simplifies the small state-update circuit following the existing local
comparison. Those timing reports describe r4s1, not a verified critical
path of r5s0; whether counter updates still limit the winner must be
established in the matched implementation evaluation.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Re-encode only each row's two-bit saturating direction counter as a
three-bit thermometer register q[2:0]. Logical counts 0, 1, 2, and 3
map respectively to 000, 001, 011, and 111. Fetch uses q[1] directly
for taken prediction, preserving the current threshold without a
binary conversion or extra lookup logic. A taken hit increments by
shifting in one: {q[1:0], 1'b1}. A not-taken hit decrements by shifting
in zero: {1'b0, q[2:1]}. These operations saturate intrinsically.
A jump sets 111; a taken miss allocates 011. A not-taken miss,
invalidation, and absence of a pending event retain the counter.

Express counter next state as parallel Boolean data terms, followed
by an unconditional clocked assignment, rather than arithmetic or
nested conditional writes. Specifically, let E be pending_valid_q
AND !reset and H be the existing valid-qualified full-tag row_hit.
Define J = E AND command_is_JUMP, A = E AND command_is_TAKEN AND !H,
U = E AND command_is_TAKEN AND H, D = E AND command_is_NOT_TAKEN AND H,
and K = !(J OR A OR U OR D). Use bitwise equations:
  next_q[2] = J | (U & q[1]) | (K & q[2]);
  next_q[1] = J | A | (U & q[0]) | (D & q[2]) | (K & q[1]);
  next_q[0] = J | A | U | (D & q[1]) | (K & q[0]).
Decode the pending command locally and retain a single sequential
owner for each counter. Allocation terms must produce known constants
even when the old, invalid counter payload is uninitialized. Counter
payloads need no reset: reset suppresses updates and the existing
valid reset masks them until a complete legal allocation.

The intended mapped circuit has no saturation detection or binary
arithmetic and no tag-dependent counter CE, SET, or RESET input.
Hit qualification and self-retention are represented in the data
equations. Inspect the mapped netlist to verify this property: an
equivalent rewrite that synthesis folds back into hit-qualified
counter enables does not establish the intended optimization. Do not
introduce device primitives, synthesis-only behavior, or blanket keep
attributes to force a result. The source-level cost is just sixteen
additional counter bits; actual mapped LUT/FF cost must be measured.

Preserve the sixteen rows, full 26-bit tags, exact tag comparisons,
valid/tag update logic, separate indexed target store, all private
pending events, and the existing capture/commit edges. Commit against
current row state, including consecutive events and different tags
aliasing one row. Keep matching-only invalidation and not-taken updates,
target retention, reset cancellation, and once-only pending-event drain
through stalls and redirects. Fetch still observes committed state
with the same pre-edge semantics and no update bypass. This is a
counter-encoding and logic-mapping micro-optimization, with identical
prediction policy, capacity, training latency, and instruction timing.

Estimate an unmeasured four-percent fitness improvement through Fmax
alone. For identical ELF and ready schedules, require identical public
IF predictions, accepted memory transactions, valid RVFI retirements
with their cycle positions, and marker-bracketed cycles. Confidence is
medium: full-tag equality remains, valid-bit update or EX paths may
become limiting, and added data gating may worsen routing or be
remapped into the original enable structure.

Run the unchanged lint, unit, formal, stalled cosim, and three-seed
FPGA gates. Compare against the current winner with the same tools,
ELF, and bus-ready schedules; report critical paths and LUT4/FF cost.
Compute fitness from full-precision iterations/bracketed-cycles times
median Fmax. Historical notes identify 388.66's scored workload as
2 KB; keep that comparison separate from the requested canonical 6 KB
run, verifying d4b0/be52/5e47 CRCs, memory bounds, both timing markers,
and the validation UART literal without altering evaluation files.
Preserve nret=1, external IO, RVFI order and traps, decoder legality,
memory handshakes, all M-extension/ALTOPS logic, and every invariant.

title: Separate predictor tag validation from ordered metadata commit
motivation:
The current bench winner scores 388.66 iter/s at 163.83 MHz. Its
predictor already captures resolution events into private row registers,
but each row still combines a 26-bit tag comparison, command decoding,
counter selection, and metadata write control within one clock period.
Registering the comparison result would divide this remaining maintenance
path without adding an instruction stage or extending EX recovery.

The structural history supports this specific timing direction:
hyp-20260905-002-r3s1 separated indexed row reads from updates, and
hyp-20260905-002-r4s1 raised median Fmax from 147.75 to 156.62 MHz by
capturing events before row-local updates. The latter's implementation
history identifies local tag-to-counter-enable paths in two routed seeds.
These are historical bottlenecks, not a claim that a current route has
been reproduced. The winning r5s0 subsequently reduced ID/EX recovery
fanout. In contrast, structural r5s1 lost 29.62% fitness after changing
raw IF transport and validity masking, and r1s1 store buffering saved
only 0.75% of cycles. Further partitioning maintenance work is therefore
the most promising structural experiment while retaining the winning
instruction pipeline and its bubble-control implementation.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one register boundary between row-local tag validation and predictor
metadata commit in rtl/if_stage.sv. This is one structural retiming of
the existing training transaction. Retain the sixteen direct-mapped rows,
PC[5:2] index, full PC[31:6] tags, aligned 30-bit targets, two-bit counter
policy, allocation rules, and committed-state-only fetch lookup.

Use three edges for an accepted event E. At edge N, the existing private
row capture records E's tag and command. At edge N+1, transfer that event
into a new commit register and capture one hit bit computed against the
row's logical tag/valid state AFTER the older event committing on that
same edge. At edge N+2, apply E using its registered hit, command, and
tag, together with the row's then-current two-bit counter. The existing
design commits at N+1, so this adds exactly one training-visibility cycle.
Capture, validate, and commit must overlap at one event per clock,
including an uninterrupted stream of resolutions to the same row.

Resolve the validation-stage read-after-write hazard locally. Let C be
the older event currently in this row's commit register and P the event
in its existing pending register. Compute two full-width comparisons in
parallel: table_tag == P.tag and C.tag == P.tag. If C.valid and C.command
is JUMP or TAKEN, P's effective hit is the second comparison because C
allocates or refreshes a valid row with C.tag on the validation edge.
Otherwise, if C.valid, C.command is INVALIDATE, and C.hit is true, P's
effective hit is false because C clears the row. In all other cases use
table_valid && (table_tag == P.tag). Register this effective hit with P.
Selection between comparator results is narrow; do not mux a 26-bit
effective tag ahead of one equality comparator. All forwarding is private
to the row and concerns tag/valid state only. No live resolve input or
indexed metadata read may enter the validation or commit datapath.

At commit, use the registered hit without re-comparing tags. JUMP writes
valid=1, the event tag, target, and counter=11. TAKEN writes valid=1,
the event tag and target, and counter=10 on a registered miss or a
saturating increment of the current counter on a registered hit.
NOT_TAKEN decrements the current counter with saturation only on a
registered hit and retains tag, valid, and target. INVALIDATE clears
valid only on a registered hit. Preserve the current field-specific
update policy. Do not snapshot or forward the counter into validation:
in-order commits ensure the current counter already includes all older
events. This avoids a new counter-update feedback bypass. After the
pipeline drains, every table field must equal sequential application of
the accepted resolution stream, even for alternating full-tag aliases.

Add a matching second delay register to the single indexed target-write
path, carrying target-valid, index, and target. The target and its metadata
must become visible on the same N+2 edge, including consecutive writes
to the same index with different tags or JALR destinations. Do not let a
newer target become visible under an older committed tag. The estimated
extra state is 16*(1 valid + 26 tag + 2 command + 1 hit) plus
(1 valid + 4 index + 30 target), or 515 source-level bits before mapping.

Refresh both event-stage validity bits every clock independently of IF
stalls, memory holds, divide waits, and younger redirects. An accepted
older event commits once even if instruction execution subsequently
stalls. Keep EX resolve_valid qualification unchanged so held instructions
cannot enqueue repeatedly. Reset clears every table-valid and both stages
of event/target validity, suppresses commit, and prevents pre-reset work
from repopulating the table. Invalid pipeline payload is never consulted
without its corresponding validity qualification.

Keep the architectural instruction pipeline unchanged: no fetch bypass
from pending events, no training backpressure, no delayed EX redirect,
and no change to the exact predicted_next_pc captured with an instruction.
Recovery still compares that prediction with the resolved architectural
destination and has the existing one-younger-slot penalty. Warm loops
must retain one-instruction-per-cycle throughput; cold or rapidly changing
branches can incur another miss because training becomes visible later.
Preserve IF's instruction-to-NOP behavior, the r5s0 split of ID/EX control
and payload updates, forwarding retention, load-use and bus interlocks,
and the real/ALTOPS multiplier and eight-edge divider schedules.

Predict an unmeasured four-percent fitness gain from higher median Fmax
with nearly unchanged CoreMark cycles. The added alias comparator,
roughly 515 extra state bits, placement changes, and delayed training
can erase that gain; inspect all three post-route paths to determine
whether tag comparison is actually separated from counter write control.
Do not add keep constraints, predictor-policy changes, or frontend
redesigns to this experiment. Success is a higher exact
iterations/bracketed-cycles times three-seed median Fmax than the incoming
winner under the identical workload, toolchain, and evaluation settings.

Run the unchanged lint, cocotb, formal, stalled cosim, and FPGA gates.
Preserve nret=1 and all top-level ports, strict channel-0 retirement order,
decoder legality and traps, memory bounds, stable stalled requests, and
exactly-once MMIO/marker accesses. Existing history distinguishes the
scored 2 KB run underlying 388.66 from the required canonical 6 KB run;
report like-for-like results separately without altering the evaluator.
Also validate the unchanged 6 KB, -O3, ten-iteration workload with both
bus stalls, CRCs d4b0/be52/5e47, Correct operation validated., and timing
strictly between start/stop marker handshakes. All hard invariants and
protected files remain intact.

title: Eight-bit partial tags for the target predictor
motivation:
Predictor timing has delivered substantially more fitness than the recent
accuracy additions. The r2s2 two-way table lost 7.32%, and the r5s2 return
stack saved only 0.17% of scored cycles while losing 3.98% fitness. The
successful r4s1 event pipeline isolated live EX feedback, but two routed
seeds then had local stored-tag/pending-tag paths into counter enables.
That comparison still spans 26 bits in the current r5s0 RTL, whose score
is 388.66 at 163.83 MHz. Shortening predictor identity is an untried way
to reduce comparator logic, indexed fetch mux width, and register routing
without increasing capacity, adding another prediction source, or changing
the existing update latency. These historical paths motivate the proposal;
they are not a new measurement of the current winner's critical path.

in the existing 16-entry direct-mapped target predictor. Keep the index
PC[5:2]. Apply this exact partial identity consistently to fetch lookup,
row-local training comparison, stored tags, and private pending-event
tags. Use direct bit slices, with no hash, high-address qualifier, or

The table shrinks from 944 to 656 source-level state bits, and pending
events from 499 to 211 bits: 576 fewer bits in total, before synthesis.
Eight-bit equality also gives a smaller LUT4 reduction than 26-bit

FPGA mapping and routing must confirm both the storage and timing effects.

existing resolution-edge capture followed by next-edge commit. Commit
against current local state while accepting the next event, including
consecutive same-row aliases. Preserve the indexed 16x30 target store
and its aligned delayed write. Pending validity drains every edge through
fetch stalls, backend holds, and redirects; reset cancels pending work
and clears table validity. Lookup uses committed state only, with the
pre-edge prediction selected on a commit edge and no update bypass.

Retain all counter rules under the new partial-tag match: jumps allocate
strongly taken; taken conditional misses allocate weakly taken and hits
saturating-increment; not-taken hits saturating-decrement while retaining
the target, and misses do nothing. Non-control or trapping resolutions
invalidate a partial-tag hit and never allocate. Legal target writes and
their metadata become visible together. Train only on the existing valid,
advancing EX resolution pulse, never repeatedly during memory/divide waits.

ranges or assume that high PC bits are zero. Preserve EX's exact full-width
actual_next_pc versus accepted predicted_next_pc comparison for EVERY
advancing instruction, including non-controls, illegal instructions,
completed divides, and JALR target changes. Recovery must still kill the
younger slot before it can retire or issue a data access. Preserve recovery
priority over imem stalls, deferred resolution during backend holds, and
resolved architectural RVFI next PC. No top-level IO, nret=1, decoder,
trap, forwarding, memory, or M-extension behavior changes are proposed.

unmeasured. Extra alias recoveries or a different routing bottleneck can
erase the clock gain. Compare the current winner and candidate using the
same ELF, ready schedule, toolchain, and three P&R seeds. Report bracketed
cycles, recovery counts, median Fmax, LUT4/FF cost, and critical endpoints.

run with d4b0/be52/5e47 CRCs and Correct operation validated. The historical
implementation notes identify the logged scores as 2 KB results; keep
that like-for-like score comparison separate from 6 KB throughput without
changing either benchmark or any evaluation-contract file.

title: Predecode the multiply-high result class before execute
motivation:
The current winner scores 388.66 at 163.83 MHz. Saved baseline RTL in
.tmp/thermometer-r6s0/baseline/cores/bench/rtl matches every current bench
RTL file byte-for-byte, and its generated/pnr_seed{1,2,3}/nextpnr.log
reports reproduce 163.83, 155.33, and 168.55 MHz. In seeds 1 and 3 the
critical path starts at ID/EX alu_op[4] and alu_op[2], respectively,
and ends at EX/MEM alu_result[25], taking 6.10 and 5.93 ns. Inspection
of the corresponding synth.json LUT truth table identifies the first
decode term as exactly op in {12,13,14}: MULH, MULHU, and MULHSU.
This is current-source timing evidence for result-class decoding,
rather than an assumption that predictor metadata still limits Fmax.

The prior r2s0 full nineteen-bit ALU predecode lost 3.92 percent after
exposing recovery fanout; r5s0 subsequently isolated that wide payload
control. The recent r6s0 counter rewrite, r6s1 additional predictor
update stage, and r6s2 shortened tags all regressed. This proposal
targets only the measured multiply-high class term with one additional
instruction bit and leaves the rest of ALU operation decoding intact.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move the single predicate dec_alu_op == ALU_MULH ||
dec_alu_op == ALU_MULHU || dec_alu_op == ALU_MULHSU across the ID/EX
register. Add a mul_high_sel bit to id_ex_t, preferably at its most
significant end so existing lower field positions remain stable.
Capture this predicate in ID with the control group: reset or flush
clears it, a backend stall holds it, and ordinary capture updates it
from dec_alu_op. Keep one sequential owner. Preserve the existing
independent wide-payload update rules and the five-bit ALU encoding.
Do not use the auxiliary bit to determine instruction legality.

Wire the registered bit through EX into an additional internal ALU
input. Factor only the multiply-high contribution out of the main
result case. Keep all current integer, MUL-low, and DIV/REM case arms
and default-zero behavior in a non_high_result path; omit the three
high-product arms there, so that path is zero for their opcodes.
Select the high-product candidate using only op[1:0], whose current
mapping is 00=MULH, 01=MULHU, 10=MULHSU, with 11 producing zero.
Combine the two disjoint contributions as

The registered class bit directly enables the high-result term;
do not reconstruct its five-bit opcode comparison in EX or qualify

registered bit and opcode must agree, including bubbles and holds.

Preserve the existing signed/unsigned product expressions, widths,
and bit slices. In RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, the same suboperation mapping

implementation_notes:
Implemented the multiply-high predecode hypothesis in the four proposed bench RTL files. `id_ex_t.mul_high_sel` is the new most-significant bit (230); all previous field positions and the five-bit ALU encoding remain unchanged. ID owns its only sequential assignment alongside ctrl/valid: reset or flush clears it, a backend hold preserves it, and normal capture records membership in MULH/MULHU/MULHSU independently of validity. The independent wide-payload update block is unchanged.

EX wires that register directly to the internal ALU. The main result case retains integer operations, MUL-low, DIV/REM and default zero. Only the three high-product arms move to a case on op[1:0], with 11 returning zero. The final result is the requested OR of non_high_result and the selector-masked high_result. All signedness, product widths/slices, ALTOPS constants and add/sub formulas remain exact. The divider, eight-edge schedule, forwarding, prediction, decoder/trap rules, RVFI ports, and nret=1 are unchanged.

Tests now drive the new ALU input at every opcode change, including reset and rejected/perturbed divide requests. Added alternating result classes with signed boundary operands, all reserved ALU default-zero opcodes, high multiplication while the divider is occupied, ID control/hold priority combinations (including flush+hold and invalid captures), and whole-pipeline selector/op assertions before and after every edge. Directed real and ALTOPS pipeline tests cover all high operations, EX/MEM and MEM/WB forwarding, dependent stalled loads, load-use bubbles, redirects with instruction stalls, divide waits and reset of both held live instructions and nonzero bubbles. Existing assertions were retained.

Local verification:

- Exact requested Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings or errors.
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider cores/bench/test/`: PASS, 10 pytest runners, including real and ALTOPS ALU tests and the additional ALTOPS high-multiply pipeline tests.
- Local formal: PASS, 53 passed / 0 failed, no RTL fix attempts. The first invocation stopped before generating checks because the default Python lacked PyYAML. Selecting the installed conda Python on PATH allowed the unchanged `formal/run_all.sh` to auto-detect nret=1 and run wrapper_si/checks_si. The script and framework were copied into bench scratch space to avoid writing into the shared protected formal tree. Full run evidence: `cores/bench/.tmp/mul-high-select/candidate/formal-gate.log`.
- Unchanged cosim gate: PASS for selftest and default 2 KB CoreMark. Additional selftest cosim against the unchanged Python ISS passed with both bus stalls for ready seeds 0xDEADBEEF, 1 and 42 (115 retirements each).
- Three unchanged FPGA routing gates: PASS. Candidate seeds 1/2/3 = 149.12 / 144.63 / 147.73 MHz; median = 147.73 MHz. Mapped resources: 6,632 LUT4, 3,203 DFF.

An observation-only scratch copy of the unchanged C++ harness emitted binary records for every cycle's prediction/readiness/acceptance/redirect/divide-wait state, accepted instruction and data bus transactions, and every field of every valid RVFI retirement including its cycle. title: Move PC-relative address generation across the ID/EX boundary
motivation:
The current bench winner reaches 388.66 iter/s at 163.83 MHz. Execute
still computes PC+4 and PC+immediate, and AUIPC selects PC onto the
shared ALU operand bus before arithmetic and result selection. These
calculations depend only on instruction metadata already available in
decode, so their register boundary can move without delaying execution
or changing branch prediction.

LESSONS.md and the structural experiment history favor a different
partition from further predictor-maintenance staging. Structural r6s1
added tag-validation staging but fell to 97.20 MHz with almost unchanged
cycles. Structural r5s1 exposed PC-to-EX/MEM ALU critical paths in all
three seeds; the r6s2 lesson also reports full-width target generation
into pending_target_q.D as critical. These are observations on related
candidates, not a reproduced timing diagnosis of the current winner.
No recorded bench hypothesis has moved PC-relative arithmetic into ID.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retime the operand-independent PC arithmetic from EX into the existing
decode-to-execute register. Add exactly two 32-bit ID/EX payload fields:
pc_plus4 = in.pc + 32'd4 and pc_relative = in.pc + decoded immediate,
both computed modulo 2^32 in id_stage. Retain the original PC, immediate,
instruction, operands, and exact predicted_next_pc. This is one
structural redistribution of work across an existing pipeline boundary;
it adds no instruction stage, issue bubble, or training stage.

Give both new fields the same update discipline as the winning r5s0
payload: deterministic zero on reset, hold only on the existing backend
stall, and otherwise capture with the rest of the instruction payload.
Flush continues to clear every control bit and valid independently of
payload capture. Preserve flush-versus-hold priority and the current IF
instruction-to-NOP behavior. Compute the sums in parallel with register
reads and control decode; no register operand or forwarding selection
belongs in either sum. A held instruction must retain its own sums
even when the live fetch data, prediction, or immediate changes.

In EX, use registered pc_relative for branch targets, direct JAL
targets, and the AUIPC writeback result. Use registered pc_plus4 for
JAL/JALR link values and the default architectural next PC, including
not-taken branches, traps, ordinary instructions, and completed divides
recovering from stale predictions. Preserve full-width target bits
until the existing alignment checks; never round a misaligned direct
target into a legal one.

Remove the is_auipc ? PC : rs1 selection from the shared ALU A input:
ordinary ALU and M-extension operations take the existing forwarded
rs1, while AUIPC selects its registered pc_relative at the EX result
selection beside the jump-link selection. Thus ID/EX PC no longer
drives the common ALU operand arithmetic, and direct-target calculation
no longer adds a carry chain before EX recovery or predictor-event
capture. Keep the existing ALU B selection and all ALU operations.

JALR remains in EX, using the actual post-forward rs1 plus the held
immediate and clearing bit zero exactly as today. Its base must not
come from an early regfile snapshot. Branch conditions also stay in EX
with existing operand forwarding. Keep misalignment/trap qualification,
result-write suppression, resolved pc_next, and the exact comparison
against the prediction accepted with that instruction. Predictor row
organization, full tags, counters, event timing, and target commit are
unchanged. Resolve and retire each advancing instruction exactly once.

Expect an unmeasured five-percent fitness improvement from shorter EX
arithmetic and control paths with identical instruction scheduling.
Risks are a new decode-immediate-adder critical path, the extra result
selection for AUIPC, roughly 64 extra payload bits before mapping, and
unchanged predictor or JALR paths limiting Fmax. This experiment must
stand on its own; retain the present frontend, predictor, arithmetic
engines, forwarding, load-use interlock, and bus-hold protocol.

then run the unchanged lint, formal, stalled cosim, and FPGA gates.

instruction streams and bus-ready sequences. Inspect all three routed

bottleneck. Compare exact iterations/bracketed cycles times three-seed
median Fmax against the incoming winner using the identical ELF and
evaluation settings; do not use the rounded core.yaml iterations/cycle
value. Record the working-set configuration, keeping the historical
scored workload and any separate canonical 6 KB run distinct. Validate
the required 6 KB, -O3, ten-iteration run with both bus stalls, CRCs
d4b0/be52/5e47, and the literal Correct operation validated.

Preserve nret=1 and the entire external port contract, channel-0 RVFI
order and operand values, decoder legality and trap checks, memory
bounds and side-effect ordering, and start/stop marker handshakes.
Real and ALTOPS arithmetic, including the eight-edge divider schedule,
are unchanged. Only bench RTL and its permitted unit tests are targets;

title: Eight-entry target predictor with shorter lookup and less training fanout
motivation:
The remaining prediction-accuracy opportunity is small relative to FPGA
timing sensitivity. Saved r6s2 measurements of the current winner show
550409 recoveries in 30822790 bracketed cycles for canonical 6 KB CoreMark.
The r5s2 return stack removed canonical-return recoveries but saved only
0.188% of those cycles, while frequency loss made fitness worse. The
two-way predictor, extra metadata-validation stage, thermometer counters,
and partial tags also regressed. In particular, partial tags reduced
storage without reducing the number of rows or target-selection inputs,
and exposed a slower EX-to-target-capture path.

Test a capacity-for-frequency trade instead: halve the direct-mapped
table itself. This reduces the depth of indexed reads and the number of
private training destinations while retaining exact tags and the proven
event pipeline. The inspected history contains no eight-entry target-table
experiment; the earlier eight-entry structure was a return stack.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the current sixteen-entry target predictor with exactly eight
direct-mapped entries. Use PC[4:2] for both fetch and resolution indices
and the complete remaining PC[31:5] as the 27-bit tag. Bit 5 moves from
the index into the tag; it is not discarded. Keep full target[31:2]
storage, two-bit saturating counters, and the current fetch equation:
a valid full-tag hit with counter[1] set selects the stored aligned
target, otherwise select PC+4. Introduce no hash, associativity, return
stack, instruction predecode, additional fetch stage, or update bypass.

Preserve the existing private resolution-event registers and their
capture-at-N, commit-at-N+1 schedule, now for eight rows. Each event
commits against its row's current state, so consecutive resolutions
with identical or conflicting tags remain ordered without forwarding.
Legal taken branches allocate weakly taken on a miss or increment a hit;
jumps allocate strongly taken. Both write the resolved aligned target.
Not-taken branches decrement matching counters without replacing targets
or allocating on a miss. Non-controls and traps invalidate only matching
full tags. Keep the delayed indexed target write atomic with metadata.
Pending validity refreshes every clock, independent of frontend/backend
holds, and reset cancels pending events and invalidates every row.

The intended hardware change is an eight-input rather than sixteen-input
indexed read for tags, counters, and targets, with half as many private
row destinations for resolution feedback. Source-level table state falls
from 944 to 480 bits; event state falls from 499 to 274 bits, a combined
reduction of 689 bits before synthesis. The extra tag bit preserves full
address discrimination. Inspect the synthesized mapping and routed paths
to establish whether the shorter selection network and lower feedback
fanout actually improve timing; storage savings alone are not evidence.

This deliberately changes prediction residency and may increase conflict
recoveries. The current residual-recovery count does not bound the new
misses caused by downsizing. Estimate an unmeasured three-percent net
fitness improvement, with low confidence: reduced routing and lookup cost
must outweigh the measured cycle penalty, and the winner already has
competing EX datapath and recovery critical paths. Do not truncate tags,
retime training, or add another predictor mechanism to rescue the result.

Keep exact accepted predicted_next_pc capture and EX comparison for every
advancing instruction. Predictions remain advisory; architectural next
PC, full addresses, JALR target changes, traps, wrong-path suppression,
once-only training through memory/divide holds, and instruction-stall
recovery priority retain their current semantics. Preserve nret=1,
every external port, decoder legality, M-extension/ALTOPS behavior,
all invariants, and all evaluation files.

Evaluate the candidate against the current winner using identical ELFs,
tools, and ready schedules, the unchanged correctness gates, and median
Fmax from all three FPGA seeds. Measure bracketed cycles and recoveries
by control-flow class, plus LUT4/FF use and critical-path endpoints.
Compute fitness as iterations divided by bracketed cycles times median
Fmax in Hz, retaining full precision. A cycle increase of fraction c
requires a frequency increase greater than c to improve the product.

that comparison separately from canonical 6 KB throughput. For 6 KB,

title: Select forwarded JALR targets after parallel operand additions
motivation:
The current bench winner scores 388.66 at 163.83 MHz. The r7s0
multiply-high predecode regressed 9.83 percent after exposing the same
path in all three routed seeds: EX/MEM destination-register comparison,

title: Retime operand dependency matching across the ID/EX boundary
motivation:
The current forwarding path compares two five-bit EX source addresses
against both downstream destination registers, resolves writer priority,
and selects operands before ALU arithmetic, branch comparison, and JALR
target generation. The r7s0 implementation notes identify EX/MEM rd
through forwarding and the JALR adder into pending_target_q as the worst
path in all three candidate seeds. The r4s0 lesson also exposed forwarding
before branch comparison. These are related-candidate measurements, not
proof that forwarding is the incoming winner's worst path: the reproduced
winner instead has ALU-control and prediction-recovery endpoints.

The structural history includes store decoupling, divider separation,
predictor-event pipelines, recovery distribution, and PC-adder retiming,
but no retiming of operand dependency comparisons. Further predictor
validation stages and PC precomputation regressed substantially. Test
moving dependency detection across an existing instruction boundary:
the incoming instruction's sources and its two preceding destinations
are already available before ID/EX capture. Four registered comparison
bits can remove address equality from the execute operand path without
increasing instruction latency or registering a wide forwarded value.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split forwarding into early address matching and late write qualification.
Move only the four source/destination equality comparisons into decode
and capture their results with the instruction in ID/EX. Preserve the
existing pipeline stages, instruction acceptance schedule, data bypass
sources, and execute-stage operand muxes.

For each incoming raw source field s, compute two independent bits from
pre-edge state:
  match_ex = (s != 0) && (s == current_id_ex.rd)
  match_wb = (s != 0) && (s == current_ex_mem.rd)
The current ID/EX instruction becomes the EX/MEM producer when the
consumer is accepted; the current EX/MEM instruction becomes its MEM/WB
producer. Use the same IF instruction source fields as today's decode,
including the existing NOP substitution. Compare both fields even for
instructions that do not architecturally consume both, preserving the
existing operand/RVFI convention and load-use detector behavior.

Add exactly four match bits to the ID/EX payload. Reset them to zero;
otherwise capture whenever the existing ID/EX payload captures, and hold
whenever stall_id holds that payload. Follow the winning r5s0 separation:
flush clears all controls and valid, without adding flush to these
payload registers' reset or enable. Matches captured in a bubble are
inert. A later accepted instruction always receives newly computed bits.

In the following execute cycle, select EX/MEM when its registered match
bit and current EX/MEM ctrl.reg_write are both true. Otherwise select
MEM/WB when its independent registered match bit and current MEM/WB
ctrl.reg_write are true; otherwise use the original ID/EX operand value.
Keep the existing 00/01/10 selector encoding and EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB
priority. Do not resolve priority before capture: a matching younger
producer can have its write suppressed by a trap, in which case the
matching older producer must remain available. Qualifying with the
actual downstream control registers preserves both execute- and
memory-stage alignment-trap suppression without a new combinational
trap-feedback path into the early comparisons. Source zero never matches.

Preserve MEM/WB forwarding independently of its retirement-valid bit.
During a data-memory hold, ID/EX and EX/MEM retain their identities and
MEM/WB retains its data/control even after valid clears. Therefore the
held match bits still refer to the correct retained producers. Keep
the existing load-use bubble: a load result is forwarded from MEM/WB,
never from the EX/MEM address. Leave register-file write-first bypass
intact so older WB values are captured normally at decode.

A divide is the deliberate exception to producer identity remaining
fixed during an ID/EX hold: older stages drain after its launch. Use
these matches only to obtain the existing once-accepted post-forward
divide operands. Retain div_rs1_q/div_rs2_q and the divider's captured
arithmetic operands through completion; never resample operands after
the producers move or relaunch the held divide. The next instruction
captures fresh matches on divide completion, including a dependency on
the divide moving into EX/MEM. Preserve the real and ALTOPS eight-edge
handshake, exactly-once advancement, and reset cancellation unchanged.

This is one structural redistribution of dependency detection across
ID/EX. The intended cut is destination-address equality before execute
operand selection; ALU arithmetic, branch/JALR resolution, predictor
organization and event timing, hazard equations, memory ordering, and
retirement stay as they are. No extra issue bubble, instruction stage,
speculative value capture, or memory bypass is introduced.

Estimate an unmeasured four-percent fitness improvement with low
confidence. Identical input streams and ready schedules should produce
identical accepted instructions, architectural traces, and scored cycle
counts, so any benefit must come from higher median Fmax. A new decode
comparison path, retained late write-control fanout, placement changes,
or the winner's competing ALU/recovery/predictor paths can erase it.
Inspect synthesis and all three routed seeds to verify that register
address equality ends at ID/EX and does not remain in the execute mux
cone. Do not add unrelated retiming or synthesis constraints to rescue
an unfavorable result.

Run the unchanged lint, cocotb, formal, stalled cosim, and FPGA gates.
Compare the candidate and incoming winner with identical ELFs, tools,
bus-ready sequences, and three-seed Fmax evaluation; calculate fitness
from exact iterations/bracketed cycles times median Fmax in Hz. Existing
notes identify 388.66 as the historical scored 2 KB result; keep that
comparison distinct from the mandatory canonical 6 KB, -O3, ten-iteration
run. Require d4b0/be52/5e47 CRCs, Correct operation validated., bounded
accesses, and timing strictly between accepted start/stop marker writes.
Preserve nret=1, every external port and RVFI field, strict channel-0
order, legality defaults, traps, all arithmetic, and every invariant.
Only bench RTL and its permitted unit tests are implementation targets.

implementation_notes:
# Operand dependency matching across ID/EX

Implemented the requested structural change. All correctness gates passed. The
measured result is a regression: median Fmax fell from 163.83 to 153.80 MHz
(-6.1222%), with identical benchmark marker cycles. The candidate remains in
place for the orchestrator; no unrelated retiming or constraints were added.

## Implementation

- Added exactly four bits to `id_ex_t`: `rs1_match_ex`, `rs1_match_wb`,
  `rs2_match_ex`, and `rs2_match_wb`. Other pipeline bundle declarations are
  unchanged.
- `id_stage` compares each raw, nonzero IF source field with the pre-edge
  ID/EX and EX/MEM destinations. Both age matches are independent; neither
  validity, producer write eligibility, priority, nor trap feedback qualifies
  these comparisons. Existing IF NOP substitution remains in effect.
- Matches reset to zero and capture with the existing ID/EX payload when
  `!stall`. Flush still clears only controls/valid. Simultaneous flush and
  hold preserves the match payload.
- `forward_unit` uses registered matches and the actual EX/MEM and MEM/WB
  `ctrl.reg_write` fields. Selectors remain 00/01/10, with EX/MEM priority and
  MEM/WB fallback when the younger write is suppressed. MEM/WB retirement
  valid and `wb_stage.w_en` do not qualify forwarding.
- `core` wires producer destinations into decode and matches into forwarding.
  The existing execute operand muxes are unchanged.
- Divider launch, captured arithmetic operands, `div_rs1_q`/`div_rs2_q`, result
  consumption, eight-edge real/ALTOPS timing, reset cancellation, and pipeline
  drain behavior are unchanged. Hazards, register-file write-first bypass,
  memory ordering, prediction/recovery, retirement, nret=1, and external ports
  are unchanged.

The only change to `ex_stage.sv` is a local UNUSEDSIGNAL annotation documenting
that the four new input bundle bits are consumed by the separate forwarding
unit. This resolves Verilator's unused-bits warning without changing logic.

## Unit tests

Existing assertions were preserved and augmented:

- Updated the ID/EX unpacker and payload checks for all four fields.
- Extended the reset/flush/stall matrix with independently driven producer
  destinations and predicted match values.
- Exhausted all 32^3 source/younger/older address triples for both raw source
  fields, including x0 and simultaneous matches. Changed live instructions,
  data, and destinations during repeated holds and flush+hold; reset also
  clears a held payload with all four matches set.
- Exhausted late match/write qualification combinations, including removal
  and restoration of the younger writer's eligibility.
- Added a live-address forwarding oracle at operand consumption and an
  architectural register scoreboard checking both raw RVFI operands at every
  retirement, including unused source fields.
- Added every-register immediate/one-gap dependencies, repeated writes,
  ALU/all multiply forms, branch/JALR, store base/data, loads, and EX/MEM trap
  suppression. Misaligned JAL/JALR tests explicitly require the independent
  older match to remain usable; misaligned loads retain the load-use bubble
  and fall back to the captured register-file value.
- Added exact accepted marker-write schedules with repeated memory holds and
  forwarding from MEM/WB after valid clears. Existing imem-bubble, redirect,
  wrong-path, prediction, memory, and reset assertions remain active.
- Strengthened divide checks to compare retained RVFI operand snapshots
  throughout older-stage draining. Added real and ALTOPS pipeline runs covering
  a divide behind stalled memory, consecutive divides, immediate consumers,
  and reset during division, all with exactly-once eight-edge handshakes.

## Local gates

The incoming bench RTL was copied before any edits. Builds and gate outputs
were isolated under `$TMPDIR/operand-retime-7q7ly7a6/`, with `incoming/` and
`candidate/` trees. Protected harnesses were copied without modification;
the shared riscv-formal checkout was not used as a writable build directory.

- Required command `verilator --lint-only -Wall -Wno-MULTITOP -sv
  +incdir+cores/bench/rtl cores/bench/rtl/*.sv`: PASS, no warnings.
- Candidate `make test TARGET=bench`: PASS, all 12 pytest runners, including
  real and ALTOPS arithmetic and pipeline runs. The incoming suite passed all
  9 runners. The final additional all-matches reset assertion passed in a
  subsequent targeted ID-stage run.
- `CORE_NAME=bench RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh`:
  candidate PASS, 53 passed / 0 failed on the first attempt, zero RTL fix
  attempts. Incoming PASS, 53 passed / 0 failed. Single-channel wrapper and
  ALTOPS configuration were selected from unchanged `nret: 1`.
- `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`: PASS on both designs, selftest ISS cosim
  and stalled 2 KB CoreMark CRC gate.
- Additional unchanged-harness stalled cosim: one common selftest ELF and
  one common dependency ELF, with both `--istall --dstall` and seeds 1, 7, 97.
  All six comparisons passed the unchanged Python ISS comparison. Complete

title: Train bimodal direction counters independently of target tags
motivation:
The current predictor qualifies direction-counter updates and taken-miss
initialization with a 26-bit row-tag comparison. Recent r7s1 and r7s2
results still identify row-counter paths among the routed bottlenecks.
Reducing capacity, shortening tags, thermometer encoding, and adding a
tag-validation pipeline stage all regressed in the inspected history.
The current winner reaches 388.66 fitness at 163.83 MHz, so a useful
predictor change must improve the clock/cycle product, not just accuracy
or source-level storage. Decoupling direction training from target
identity removes the wide comparison from the counter's dependencies
without adding a fetch selection level or changing target capacity.
This policy change has not been tried in the recorded experiments.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Convert the sixteen existing two-bit direction counters into an untagged,
PC-indexed bimodal direction table while retaining the sixteen-entry,
full-tag direct-mapped target table. Both still use PC[5:2]; keep the
counters as private scalar registers in their existing rows. This is a
single predictor-policy experiment: direction history belongs to an
index and persists across target replacements and invalidations, rather
than belonging to the target table's resident full PC.

Reset all sixteen counters to 2'b10, independently of table validity.
At the existing pending-event commit edge, a legal JUMP sets its row's
counter to 2'b11, TAKEN saturating-increments it, and NOT_TAKEN
saturating-decrements it. Apply these counter updates regardless of
row_hit, tag_q, or valid_q, including not-taken target-table misses and
taken allocations. INVALIDATE and absent events leave the counter alone.
There is no special weakly-taken initialization on target allocation.
Counter initialization is necessary because a not-taken event can now
train an index that has never held a valid target.

Give each binary counter one sequential owner separate from target
metadata updates. Counter next data and write qualification may depend
only on its current two bits, the row's registered pending command and
validity, and reset. Remove all tag-match and target-valid dependencies
from that cone; do not merely move their qualification from a clock
enable to a data mux. Preserve binary saturation rather than repeating
the thermometer experiment. Inspect synthesized and routed logic to
verify the intended removal of tag-to-counter D/enable paths.

Keep the fetch equation exactly as it is: a valid PC[31:6] tag match
AND counter[1] selects the stored full target[31:2], otherwise PC+4.
Thus an untagged direction alias alone cannot produce a target hit for
a different full PC. No instruction decode, hash, jump-type bypass,
associativity, global history, return stack, or additional lookup stage
is added. The table and pending-event source-level bit counts remain
944 and 499 respectively; only the 32 counter bits gain explicit reset.
Actual LUT/FF cost and timing remain measurement questions.

Preserve the target table's existing policy independently: legal jumps
and taken branches write valid, full tag, and aligned resolved target;
not-taken branches retain target metadata and never allocate; non-control
or trapping resolutions invalidate only a matching full tag. Legal
status still comes from EX after its target-alignment checks. Retain
the private per-row event capture and the aligned indexed target write:
an event captured at edge N commits at N+1, against current local state.
Consecutive aliases commit in order at one event per edge without a
table-read snapshot or update bypass. Metadata and target become visible
together. Pending validity drains on every edge through stalls and
redirects; reset clears validity, cancels pending work, and resets
direction history with priority over any commit.

The deliberate tradeoff is direction interference between full PCs
sharing an index. A not-taken miss can lower the resident branch's
direction confidence without evicting its target; a taken allocation
after a strongly-not-taken alias may initially remain predicted not
taken. Conversely, direction history survives target eviction. Jumps
still train strongly taken, but subsequent aliased branches can lower
that counter. Do not assume unchanged CoreMark cycles or invent an
accuracy gain. Estimate an unmeasured three-percent net fitness gain
with low confidence: eliminating the tag-qualified counter path must
repay any additional recoveries, and EX target generation or recovery
may become the limiting routed path.

Preserve the exact predicted_next_pc captured with each accepted
instruction and EX's full-width actual-next-PC comparison for every
advancing instruction, including non-controls, traps, completed divides,
and changing JALR destinations. Keep existing recovery and fetch-stall
priority, once-only resolution during memory/divide holds, wrong-path
suppression, resolved RVFI next PC, nret=1, all external ports, and all
decoder, memory, forwarding, arithmetic, and evaluation invariants.

Validate the independent predictor policy edge by edge and retain all
architectural pipeline assertions. Run the unchanged correctness and
FPGA gates, comparing identical workloads and ready schedules against
the winner with all three P&R seeds. Report bracketed cycles, recovery
counts by control-flow class, median Fmax, LUT4/FF cost, and critical
endpoints. Use full-precision iterations/bracketed-cycles times Fmax_Hz;
a fractional cycle increase c requires a frequency increase greater
than c to improve fitness. Historical notes distinguish the scored
2 KB result underlying 388.66 from canonical 6 KB throughput; report
those separately without changing the evaluator. The required 6 KB,
ten-iteration run must retain both timing markers, bounded accesses,
d4b0/be52/5e47 CRCs, and the Correct operation validated. UART literal.

implementation_notes:
# Untagged bimodal direction training

Implemented the requested predictor policy. The measured result is a regression: historical scored fitness falls from 388.659115376458 to 257.919174279941 iterations/s (-33.638717303692%). The estimated three-percent improvement was not observed. No additional predictor mechanism or evaluator change was introduced to rescue the result.

## Implementation

- `cores/bench/rtl/if_stage.sv`: each of the sixteen private binary counters has one sequential owner, separate from tagged metadata. Reset initializes every counter to `10`. A registered valid JUMP writes `11`, TAKEN saturating-increments, and NOT_TAKEN saturating-decrements, independently of tag and target validity. INVALIDATE and absent events preserve history. There is no allocation initialization.
- Target metadata still allocates on legal JUMP/TAKEN, retains its tag/target on NOT_TAKEN, and invalidates only a matching full tag. The sixteen-entry fetch equation, full tags and aligned targets, capture-at-N/commit-at-N+1 ordering, pre-edge lookup visibility, stall-independent draining, atomic target/metadata publication, reset cancellation, and PC priority are unchanged. Source-level table/event state remains 944/499 bits; the existing 32 counter bits gain reset.
- `test_if_stage.py` updates its independent public-output reference and adds all-index probes for every binary increment/decrement saturation transition, JUMP from every state, not-taken training before allocation, direction inheritance during repeated alias replacement, target retention, and matching/missing non-control and trap invalidations at every counter state. Existing continuous capture/commit, full-tag/full-target, stalls, redirects, and reset assertions remain.
- `test_pipeline.py` models direction separately from target residency. A new bounded program combines taken/not-taken PCs separated by 0x40, an initial aliased jump, changing JALR destinations, stale-code alignment/decoder traps, load-use interlocks, blocking divides, instruction stalls, and data holds. Three deterministic stalled schedules match its zero-wait architectural trace. It checks exact accepted predictions/recoveries, unique resolution and retirement, strict RVFI order/PC chaining, link/operand data, divide timing, and absence of wrong-path retirement or memory accesses using sentinel stores. The only existing directed expectation changed is cold-taken hysteresis: reset `10` increments to `11`, so the first NOT_TAKEN leaves `10`.
- Added optional `test_predictor_profile.py` for measurement. It builds an observational C++ wrapper around a verbatim include of the protected cosim harness, reads advancing EX events, checks accepted-prediction recovery and resolution/retirement correspondence, and counts recovery classes between marker handshakes. It never drives inputs. For every profiled workload, its complete stdout exactly matches the ordinary gate simulator, including final RVFI record, cycles, bounds status, and every UART byte. Generated sources/build products stay in scratch directories. It is not an alternative correctness gate.

No changes were made to external ports, nret=1, EX, decoder, forwarding, memory, arithmetic, divider, other cores, benchmark sources, or evaluation contracts. The only addition beyond the suggested three source files is the optional profiling helper. This notes file is at the explicitly requested worktree-root location consumed by the orchestrator.

- Unchanged `make test TARGET=bench`: PASS, all nine runners, including real and ALTOPS arithmetic. IF has five cocotb tests and pipeline has 38. An initial run exposed the old cold-taken expectation described above; updating that policy-specific expectation made the full gate pass. No architectural assertion was removed or weakened.

Automatic nret=1 selection used `wrapper_si.sv` and `checks_si.cfg`. No counterexample, RTL fix attempt, or formal retry was needed. `formal-deep` was not run; arithmetic RTL is unchanged and both arithmetic simulation modes passed.

title: Fold jump link values into the ALU result selection
motivation:
The current winner scores 388.66 at 163.83 MHz. The saved RTL under
.tmp/thermometer-r6s0/baseline/cores/bench/rtl matches every current
bench RTL file byte for byte. Its final nextpnr reports reproduce
163.83, 155.33, and 168.55 MHz. Seeds 1 and 3 have critical paths from
ID/EX alu_op through result selection to EX/MEM alu_result[25], taking
6.10 and 5.93 ns. The final mapped LUT on those paths also receives
is_jump: ex_stage currently selects PC+4 after the complete ALU result.
This independent selection dimension gates ordinary arithmetic results
even though a jump never needs its nominal ADD result for writeback.

LESSONS.md and the micro_opt entries were reviewed. Full registered ALU
predecode in r2s0 and multiply-high predecode in r7s0 regressed; both
retained the final link mux. The r8s0 parallel JALR adders also regressed
and left ALU result selection as the routed limit. This proposal removes
the separate link-result selection through mutually exclusive operation
encoding, without adding predecode state or duplicating target adders.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one internal five-bit operation, ALU_LINK = 5'd19, leaving all
existing operation values 0 through 18 unchanged. Within the decoder's
already validated JAL and legal JALR arms, select ALU_LINK instead of
the default ALU_ADD. Keep is_jump, is_jalr, alu_src, register-write
controls, immediate decoding, and every legality condition unchanged.
Reserved JALR encodings must retain the decoder's illegal defaults.

Give the internal alu module a 32-bit link_value input. Add ALU_LINK
as a peer arm of its existing result case, returning link_value directly.
In EX, drive link_value from the existing modulo-2^32 in.pc + 4 value
and capture alu_result directly into reg_q.alu_result for every
advancing instruction. Remove the independent is_jump ? PC+4 :
alu_result selection at this register input. Express PC+4 once for
link_value and the existing sequential-next-PC calculation. Keep the
current forwarded alu_a/alu_b selection and all branch/JAL/JALR target
arithmetic unchanged; ALU_LINK simply ignores a and b for its result.

The intended hardware improvement is one mutually exclusive result
selection network that includes the link value, replacing an ALU
network followed by a separate jump override. Do not recreate the
override inside alu, such as an outer op == ALU_LINK ternary around
the old result case. There is no new register, bundle field, pipeline
boundary, instruction latency, operand forwarding policy, or ALU-op
renumbering. The existing ctrl.alu_op field transports ALU_LINK with
exactly the current ID/EX reset, flush, and backend-hold rules.

JAL/JALR must still write their own PC+4, including rd equal to rs1
and immediate link consumers. JALR target computation must still use
the original post-forward rs1 plus the full immediate and clear bit 0.
Misaligned targets must retain their current trap, PC recovery, and
write-suppression behavior. Keep raw RVFI operands, architectural next
PC, accepted predictions, predictor training, nret=1, and external

implementation_notes:
Implemented the proposed ALU_LINK fold. Correctness checks pass, but the measured FPGA result is a regression: median Fmax falls from 163.83 MHz to 124.67 MHz (-23.90282610022584%). The implementation is left in place for the orchestrator to evaluate; the predicted three-percent gain was not observed.

The RTL change follows the hypothesis exactly. ALU_LINK is 5'd19, with operations 0 through 18 unchanged. Only the existing legal JAL and funct3=0 JALR decoder arms select it. The ALU has a 32-bit link_value input and a peer ALU_LINK result-case arm shared by real and ALTOPS builds. EX computes a single 32-bit pc_plus_4 for that input and sequential actual_next_pc, and captures alu_result directly into EX/MEM. There is no outer link override in the ALU.

No pipeline state, bundle fields, retirement width, external ports, forwarding rules, target adders, prediction/training rules, trap behavior, or sequential hold/bubble rules were changed. All integer, multiply, signed-product, ALTOPS and divider expressions and the eight-edge divider controller remain unchanged. Unsupported internal operations 20 through 31 still produce zero.

Tests now check complete legal jump and reserved-JALR decoder controls, exact LINK passthrough while alternating every result class, varying unused link inputs, all unsupported internal opcodes, and divider independence while idle, busy and retaining a result. ID tests check LINK ownership through legal/invalid captures, reset, flush, hold and simultaneous flush/hold. Pipeline additions cover dependent link consumers, rd=rs1 JALR, full signed immediates and bit-zero clearing, x0 links, forwarded/load-dependent targets, eleven-cycle data holds with retained WB forwarding, instruction stalls, divide waits, misaligned write suppression, reset and PC+4 wraparound. Existing assertions remain in place. An optional PIPELINE_TRANSCRIPT output records architectural events for comparison against the incoming RTL.

Local verification completed:

- Required Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings. ALTOPS lint also passes without warnings.
- Existing pytest unit suite: 9 runner cases passed, including both real and ALTOPS ALU builds and all 40 pipeline tests.
- Local formal: PASS, 53 passed / 0 failed, using unchanged formal/run_all.sh, wrapper_si.sv and checks_si.cfg with nret=1. No RTL fix attempts or counterexamples. An initial shell launch exited before generating checks because the default Python lacked PyYAML; selecting the already installed Miniconda Python resolved that environment issue.
- Selftest cosim against the unchanged Python ISS: PASS, 115 retirements with zero wait and with both random bus stalls. Baseline and candidate RVFI records, including cycle positions, match byte for byte in each schedule.
- All 108 pipeline runs match the incoming winner's architectural transcript byte for byte: 1,881 valid retirements, 5,635 clocked cycles, 2,086 accepted fetches, 97 accepted reads and 83 accepted writes. The transcript includes cycle positions, raw RVFI operands/results, exact accepted predictions, resolution and predictor-commit events, accepted memory data/masks and marker transactions. Deliberately cancelled pre-edge observations in reset tests are excluded from acceptance counts. Both complete pipeline suites passed again after finalizing this transcript bookkeeping.
- Full stalled CoreMark RVFI streams match byte for byte under the same ELF and default ready-sequence seed: 22,093,920 records for 6 KB, and 2,937,037 records for 2 KB. Every emitted RVFI field and its cycle position was compared, including inactive memory data fields.

The mandatory 6 KB run used the unchanged benchmark sources and Makefile with COREMARK_SIZE=6000, COREMARK_OPT=-O3 and ITERATIONS=10. Both CPUs consumed the same ELF with --istall --dstall. Start marker acceptance was cycle 53,747 and stop marker acceptance was cycle 30,876,537, giving exactly 30,822,790 bracketed cycles on both designs. Both reached EBREAK with oob=false and bench_bracketed=true, canonical crclist=d4b0, crcmatrix=be52, crcstate=5e47, and the literal "Correct operation validated." Additional observed CRCs were seedcrc=8a02 and crcfinal=5949.

All 22,093,920 six-KB retirement records were additionally checked for bounded instruction and memory addresses. The highest retired/next instruction address was 0x39e8. Memory addresses were within [0, 0x00100000), with MMIO limited to 0x10000000, 0x10000100 and 0x10000104, all within the required MMIO window. The existing C++ harness also completed without its sticky out-of-bounds flag. The protected UART compiler-description string still says -O2; the captured compiler invocation is explicitly -O3. CoreMark prints the per-algorithm size as 2000 for TOTAL_DATA_SIZE=6000. Neither protected reporting string was edited.

Unchanged synthesis and three-seed routing were run on both the incoming winner and candidate, using fpga/scripts/synth.tcl, fpga/scripts/nextpnr_run.sh, the existing constraints and the single-issue wrapper. All six routes completed normally. The fresh baseline synthesis JSON is byte-identical to the saved thermometer-r6s0 baseline, and its final routed frequencies reproduce the historical reports exactly.

title: Execute multiply-high in MEM outside the fast EX result path
motivation:
The incoming winner reaches 163.83 MHz and historical fitness 388.66.
Saved r6s0-baseline RTL matches the current bench RTL byte-for-byte;
its final routed reports reproduce 163.83, 155.33, and 168.55 MHz.
Seeds 1 and 3 run from ID/EX ALU control to EX/MEM result data in
6.10 and 5.93 ns. The r7s0 netlist investigation identifies the
multiply-high class decoder in this cone. Merely registering that
class regressed 9.83 percent: it retained the combined execution
datapath and exposed forwarding/JALR timing instead.

LESSONS.md and structural log entries were reviewed. Divider separation
successfully removed expensive arithmetic from ordinary execution;
later predictor, PC-adder, and dependency-comparison retiming failed
to improve the winner. No bench experiment has moved high-half
multiplication into the otherwise idle arithmetic capacity of MEM.
The inspected bench/programs/coremark.elf contains twelve MULHU sites,
all under core_list_init or ee_printf, and no MULH/MULHSU sites.
This static evidence suggests little direct timed dependency cost,
but does not establish dynamic frequencies for either benchmark size.
