hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move execution of MULH, MULHU, and MULHSU from EX into a dedicated
combinational multiply-high lane in MEM. Keep low-half MUL and all
ordinary integer operations in EX. This is one execution-stage
repartition: high products become available at MEM/WB instead of
EX/MEM, without adding an instruction stage or changing retirement
width. Remove high-product arithmetic and result arms from the fast
ALU rather than retaining an unused fast completion path.

Add one is_mul_high control bit, derived in ID only from a legal
decoded MULH/MULHU/MULHSU. Capture it with the existing control bundle;
reset and every bubble clear it, and backend holds retain it. In EX,
keep operand forwarding and capture the existing post-forward rs1_val
and rs2_val into EX/MEM. These existing fields become the high lane's
arithmetic operands as well as its RVFI operands. The EX ALU may emit
zero for these three internal operation codes, but that placeholder
must never be forwarded, written architecturally, or reported as the
retiring result. Keep the original instruction, operation, destination,
prediction, resolved pc_next, and trap metadata paired with operands.

Compute the selected high product only from the registered EX/MEM
operands and operation. Move the current signed/signed,
unsigned/unsigned, and signed/unsigned expressions and their exact
high-half slices into the new lane without an arithmetic redesign.
On the normal MEM/WB capture edge, select this result into alu_result
for is_mul_high; other instructions retain the existing MEM behavior.
WB, register-file write-first bypass, and RVFI then receive the final
registered result through their current paths. Do not forward the
combinational MEM multiplier output back into EX: that would recreate
a multiplier-plus-consumer path across the intended stage boundary.

Generalize the existing load-use interlock to an EX producer whose
result is late: ctrl.mem_read OR ctrl.is_mul_high. Retain the current
nonzero-rd and raw source-field comparisons. An immediately dependent
instruction holds at fetch and inserts one ID/EX bubble, exactly like
a load consumer. On its later EX cycle, it uses MEM/WB forwarding.
Qualify EX/MEM forwarding eligibility with NOT is_mul_high so the
placeholder cannot override an older correct value. Retain the
established MEM/WB forwarding qualification, including forwarding
from retained payload after retirement valid clears during a memory
hold. Do not introduce operand-use filtering in this experiment.

Independent high multiplies can occupy EX and MEM in consecutive
cycles and still retire at one instruction per cycle. A high multiply
in MEM is not a memory request and must advance even if dmemReady is
low; an older stalled load/store retains the existing backend hold.
Preserve the complete MEM/WB forwarding payload on a real memory
hold. Keep divider launch, accepted operand retention, eight-edge
real/ALTOPS schedule, older-stage draining, and result consumption
unchanged. A divide consuming a high result receives the same late
producer interlock as any other consumer. Reset, redirects, and invalid
slots cannot leave a high-operation control bit attached to another
instruction. EX recovery and predictor training retain their current
acceptance rules; high multiply resolves its architectural PC normally.

Preserve MUL-low's current ALTOPS formula in the fast ALU. Relocate
MULH=(a+b)^0xf6583fb7, MULHU=(a+b)^0x949ce5e8, and
MULHSU=(a-b)^0xecfbe137 into the MEM lane under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS,
using 32-bit modular arithmetic and the same captured operands.
Real and ALTOPS builds must use identical result availability and
interlocks. Preserve every existing high-multiply arithmetic vector
by moving its coverage to the new lane and checking integrated CPU
retirement; removing high operations from the ALU is not permission
to remove their correctness coverage or weaken formal checks.

Predict an unmeasured 5 percent fitness gain, with low confidence,
from removing high arithmetic and its selection from fast EX. The
moved lane may become MEM's critical path, separately placed low/high
multipliers may increase DSP/LUT demand, and existing recovery or
predictor paths may cap Fmax. Dependent high multiplies add bubbles;
measure their actual marker-bracketed frequency and cycle cost. Earlier
high operations can also change the random-ready phase at the start
marker, so unchanged static timed code does not imply identical cycles.
Inspect mapped and all three routed cones to confirm high arithmetic
is fed by EX/MEM registers and cannot reach the fast EX result directly.

Run unchanged lint, cocotb, formal, stalled ISS cosim, and FPGA gates.
Compare exact iterations/bracketed cycles times three-seed median
Fmax against the incoming RTL with identical ELFs and ready schedules.
History identifies 388.66 as the scored 2 KB result; keep that comparison
separate from the required canonical 6 KB, -O3, ten-iteration run.
Require d4b0/be52/5e47 CRCs, Correct operation validated., bounded
accesses, and timing strictly between accepted start/stop marker writes.
Preserve nret=1, every external port, strict channel-0 retirement order,
decoder defaults and traps, memory ordering, and all hard invariants.
Only bench RTL and its permitted unit tests are implementation targets.

title: Capture raw predictor events before update classification
motivation:
The current sixteen-entry predictor classifies each live EX resolution
into INVALIDATE/JUMP/TAKEN/NOT_TAKEN before capturing its private row
event. Classification includes target-trap legality and branch outcome;
the same late conditions also qualify the pending target register's
capture enable. This puts prediction maintenance on the execution path
even though its writes occur one edge later.

The predictor history supports shortening maintenance paths while
retaining prediction behavior: row-local training and registered events
improved fitness in r3s2 and r4s1. Conversely, r8s2 lost 33.64% after
untagged direction training increased recoveries and synthesis changed
pending commands from one-hot to binary. Its routed bottleneck crossed
forwarding and EX classification into command capture. Smaller tables,
partial tags, additional tag-validation stages, and thermometer counters
have also regressed. The proposed experiment changes where training
classification occurs, retaining the winner's tagged predictor policy.
The winner itself has competing ALU and recovery limits, so removing
this maintenance path is a hypothesis, not a guaranteed Fmax gain.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move predictor update classification across the EXISTING event-capture
boundary, without adding another stage. In each private row, replace
pending_command_q with independent registered raw fields: decoded
is_branch, decoded is_jump, resolved branch-taken, decoder legality
BEFORE EX target-alignment trapping, and target-misaligned. Capture the
last field from resolve_target[1:0] != 0, independently of outcome.
Continue capturing the full tag and row validity at the existing edge.
Every payload capture enable must remain resolve_valid && row_index_hit;
neither branch outcome nor target legality qualifies that enable.

Expose the pre-trap decoder-legality bit from EX through core to IF.
Keep EX's architectural trap generation, resolved legality, next-PC
selection, and once-only resolve_valid qualification unchanged. The
original resolved-legality signal may remain available to existing
monitors, but must not feed the new predictor capture cones.

After capture, derive the original command locally from the registered
raw fields. For decoder-produced control classes, effective legality is
decode_legal && !(target_misaligned && (jump || (branch && taken))).
An effectively illegal event or non-control becomes INVALIDATE; a legal
jump becomes JUMP; otherwise a legal branch becomes TAKEN or NOT_TAKEN.
Thus an untaken branch with a misaligned encoded destination remains
legal and can decrement a matching counter; a taken misaligned branch
or jump invalidates only its matching entry. Derive this combinationally
after the registers rather than storing another encoded command.

Apply precisely the existing row-local commit rules against current
tag/valid/counter state. JUMP sets counter 11; a TAKEN miss allocates 10,
and a TAKEN hit saturating-increments. NOT_TAKEN decrements only a tag
hit, retaining the target and never allocating. INVALIDATE clears only
a matching valid entry. Preserve all sixteen PC[5:2] rows, full 26-bit
tags, thirty-bit aligned targets, and committed-state-only fetch lookup.

Make the single indexed target path capture its raw event on every
resolve_valid, rather than only when live target_write is true. Retain
its index and target payload, and capture the same raw classification
fields alongside them. At the existing commit edge, generate its write
enable exclusively from that registered event's validity and locally
derived JUMP/TAKEN classification. This global target event and every
private metadata event must refer to the same resolution age; do not
combine a pending target with live EX fields or an indexed metadata read.
Metadata and target still publish together at N+1 for capture at N.

Capture and commit must overlap at one event per edge, including
consecutive aliases and changing JALR targets. Pending validity refreshes
every edge independently of fetch stalls, memory holds, divide waits,
and redirects, so accepted events drain exactly once. Reset clears all
table/event validity, suppresses writes, and cancels pending work. Raw
payloads need no reset because validity masks every commit and lookup.

This experiment targets the late EX classification and target-capture
enable cones; it does not change prediction accuracy or visibility.
Verify in synthesized and routed netlists that capture D pins receive
separate raw fields and that pending target capture enables no longer
depend on taken/trap classification. Derived command logic belongs only
after the register boundary. Report automatic encoding or enable
inference that defeats this separation. Added event bits, routing,
target-register switching, and competing ALU/recovery or row-counter
paths can offset the benefit. Estimate an unmeasured four-percent net
fitness gain, with low confidence.

Require identical predictions, redirect decisions, training visibility,
retirement and bus-transaction cycle positions, and bracketed CoreMark
cycles against the incoming winner for identical ELFs and ready
schedules. Preserve the exact accepted predicted_next_pc and full-width
EX mismatch recovery for every advancing instruction, including stale
non-controls, traps, and completed divides. Preserve nret=1, all external
IO, RVFI order, decoder checks, arithmetic, and every hard invariant.

Run the unchanged lint, unit, formal, stalled cosim, and three-seed FPGA
gates. Evaluate full-precision iterations/bracketed-cycles times median
Fmax_Hz, recording LUT4/FF cost and all three routed critical paths.
History identifies 388.66 with the scored 2 KB image; keep that comparison
separate from the required canonical 6 KB measurement without editing
the evaluator. Validate the 6 KB ten-iteration run with both stalls,
accepted start/stop markers, bounded accesses, CRCs d4b0/be52/5e47, and
the literal Correct operation validated. in UART output.

implementation_notes:
# Capture raw predictor events before update classification

Implemented the proposed register boundary change and retained the incoming predictor policy and cycle behavior. All correctness gates pass, and synthesis plus all three routed netlists retain the separate raw capture fields. The measured FPGA result is a regression: median Fmax is 125.47 MHz and the scored 2 KB fitness is 297.656468328659 iterations/s, versus the incoming winner's 163.83 MHz and 388.659115376458 iterations/s, a 23.414515046084% reduction. The proposed low-confidence four-percent gain is not supported by this measurement.

## Implementation

- `ex_stage.sv` exposes `resolve_decode_legal = !in.ctrl.is_illegal`. Existing architectural target traps, resolved legality, next PC, full-width prediction mismatch recovery, divide behavior, and once-only `resolve_valid` are unchanged.
- `core.sv` routes decoder legality into IF. The original `resolve_legal` remains connected to EX and visible to monitors, but does not feed predictor capture. External buses and the single-channel RVFI interface remain unchanged; `nret` remains 1.
- `if_stage.sv` replaces every private pending command register with five independent raw registers: branch, jump, taken, decoder legality, and target misalignment. Misalignment captures `resolve_target[1:0] != 0` without outcome qualification. Tag and all five fields use only `resolve_valid && resolve_index == row` as their payload capture enable.
- A combinational `classify_event` function is applied independently to each registered metadata event and to the registered target event. It implements decoder legality with outcome-qualified target trapping after capture. Untaken misaligned branches can decrement a matching row; taken misaligned branches and misaligned jumps invalidate only matching valid rows.
- The single target event captures its index, thirty target bits and five raw fields on every `resolve_valid`. Its registered validity and local JUMP/TAKEN classification drive target publication at the same N+1 edge as metadata. No live EX field or indexed metadata read participates in this decision.
- All sixteen PC[5:2] rows, full 26-bit tags, aligned 30-bit targets, tagged two-bit saturation policy, target retention on NOT_TAKEN, committed-state-only fetch lookup, overlapping capture/commit, and PC priority remain unchanged. Validity refreshes each edge regardless of holds or recovery. Reset clears table/event validity, cancels pending work, and suppresses publication. Raw payloads have no reset.

The table remains 944 source-level bits. Event state grows from 499 to 552 source-level bits: `16*(1+26+5) + (1+4+30+5)`. There is no extra pipeline stage.

## Tests and local gates

- Exact requested Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings or errors. `git diff --check`: PASS.
- Unchanged `make test TARGET=bench`: PASS, all nine runners. Existing decoder, arithmetic, ALTOPS, forwarding, retirement, and pipeline assertions remain intact.
- Local formal status: **PASS, 53 passed / 0 failed**, using unchanged `bash formal/run_all.sh` with `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl`, `CORE_NAME=bench`, and `JOBS=6`. Automatic nret=1 selection used `wrapper_si.sv` and `checks_si.cfg`. There was no formal counterexample and no RTL formal-fix attempt. `formal-deep` was not run because arithmetic RTL was unchanged.
- Unchanged `make cosim TARGET=bench NRET=1`: PASS for selftest and scored CoreMark. Additional selftest runs with both stalls, seeds 1, 2, 3 and 0xDEADBEEF, each passed the protected Python ISS comparison for all 115 retirements and matched incoming RVFI output byte-for-byte, including cycle numbers.
- Unchanged `make fpga TARGET=bench NRET=1 BENCH=fpga/core_bench_si.sv`: PASS, all three seeds routed successfully and scored CoreMark passed the unchanged evaluator.

The IF oracle continues to check public output before and after every edge. It now derives architectural legality from raw decoder legality and destination/outcome, and adds all-row alternating writes/nonwrites, misaligned taken/untaken branches, misaligned jumps, decoded illegality, colliding tags, target retention, invalid-event draining, and reset cancellation. Existing counter transitions, tag/target bit sweeps, stalls, redirects and visibility checks remain.

The pipeline oracle still trains from EX's independently observed architectural legality. It retains exact accepted-prediction, once-only resolution, strict order, PC chaining, bus and operand checks, and verifies the new decoder-legality output against the ID/EX control bundle even on holds and bubbles. New directed programs put adjacent jumps, untaken misaligned branches, decoded traps and target traps around memory holds, instruction stalls, load-use bubbles and divide completion.

Optional trace capture/comparison in `test_pipeline.py` ran the same extended suite on saved incoming RTL and the candidate: **103 runs and 5,694 cycle samples matched exactly**, including predictions, recovery cycles, training visibility, complete pipeline bundles, retirement cycles, and bus signals.

Added `test_predictor_equivalence.py` as an optional ELF comparison utility. It separately compiles the incoming and candidate cores, includes the protected cosim harness verbatim, and compares all 26 external outputs plus prediction, resolution, redirect and hold/flush signals after every evaluation on both clock phases. Both models receive identical harness inputs; a mismatch aborts immediately. This passed for selftest, scored 2 KB CoreMark, and canonical 6 KB CoreMark. The comparison simulator's complete CoreMark stdout exactly matches the ordinary harness stdout for both images. It does not replace or modify any gate.

## Tool and artifact isolation

Protected gate sources were copied unchanged beneath the supplied TMPDIR so their generated artifacts did not modify protected worktree paths. Final gate RTL and test copies were checked byte-for-byte against the delivered files. No other core, evaluator, benchmark, formal contract, FPGA contract, or core.yaml was edited. ## Synthesized and routed capture boundary

Connection and LUT truth-table checks passed on the synthesized netlist and all three routed netlists, following inserted buffers and actual register pins:

title: Suppress load-use bubbles for non-source instruction fields
motivation:
The current hazard_unit compares a load destination against both raw
instruction fields [19:15] and [24:20], regardless of instruction format.
Immediate bits can therefore create a dependency that does not exist.
For example, LW x5,0(x1) followed by ADDI x6,x2,5 inserts a bubble because
the immediate's low five bits equal x5, although ADDI only reads x2.
LUI, AUIPC, and JAL can falsely match either field despite reading no
integer source register. Removing these bubbles directly improves
iterations per cycle without adding a datapath or pipeline stage.

The bench log contains no prior source-use qualification experiment.
Earlier micro_opt attempts changed register-file selection (r1s0), ALU
selects (r2s0), JALR arithmetic selection (r8s0), and link-result selection
(r9s0), with no accepted improvement. LESSONS.md repeatedly reports
unchanged CoreMark cycles and losses from remapping or another critical
path. The accepted r5s0 control/payload separation remains valuable and
is compatible with this small change to the interlock condition.

title: Decouple fetch from decode with one fall-through instruction slot
motivation:
The current frontend discards an available instruction whenever load-use,
data-memory backpressure, or a divide prevents decode acceptance. It then
depends on io_imemReady again when execution resumes. Separating fetch
acceptance from decode acceptance can overlap these existing waits with
instruction delivery under the approximately 22 percent bus-stall workload.

LESSONS.md and the structural experiment history show that recent timing
repartitions have left CoreMark cycles unchanged while reducing Fmax:
r8s1 operand-match retiming lost 6.12 percent fitness, and r9s1 moving high
multiplication into MEM lost 18.10 percent. The earlier pending-store
experiment saved only 0.75 percent of cycles. No prior bench hypothesis
introduces an elastic fetch slot. This proposal targets instruction-supply
overlap while retaining the winner's execution and predictor organization.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add exactly one instruction holding slot inside if_stage, with a
combinational fall-through path when empty. Store only the complete
if_id_t fetch tuple: PC, instruction, exact predicted_next_pc, and validity.
Read registers and decode at actual ID acceptance, never at enqueue time.
Keep the existing ID/EX, EX/MEM, and MEM/WB stages and single retirement.

Separate the two acceptance events. Let q_valid denote slot occupancy,
available = q_valid || io_imemReady, and issue_fire mean available and
decode can accept, with neither reset nor recovery active. Decode can
accept only when the existing load-use interlock, data-memory hold, and
divide wait allow it. Let fetch_fire = io_imemReady && (!q_valid ||
issue_fire), also suppressed by reset or recovery. Only fetch_fire advances
the fetch PC to the raw fetch's prediction. Decode always selects the
stored tuple when q_valid is set, otherwise the live fetch tuple.

When empty, fetch_fire plus issue_fire transfers directly to ID without
occupying the slot or adding a cycle. When empty and decode is blocked,
fetch_fire saves the tuple and advances the fetch PC once. When occupied,
issue_fire consumes the stored instruction even if io_imemReady is zero;
simultaneous fetch_fire replaces it with the next raw fetch. An occupied
slot with no issue_fire retains every field and holds the fetch PC. Support
consume/refill on the same edge so ready buses still sustain one issue per
cycle. Neither an unready response nor an unaccepted repeated response can
overwrite the slot. Keep availability independent of downstream flushes
and acceptance so this control has no combinational ready/valid loop.

Drive hazard detection from the selected oldest instruction, not the
instruction at the now-ahead bus PC. Replace raw imem readiness in the
frontend bubble/hold equations with instruction availability. A bus stall
must not bubble a valid queued instruction. Retain the existing raw-source
load-use comparisons, backend holds, complete control clearing on bubbles,
retained MEM/WB forwarding data, and eight-edge real/ALTOPS divider behavior.
Preserve the existing NOP substitution for recovery or no available
instruction and the winning ID/EX control-versus-payload reset separation.

kills the younger decode instruction, and redirects the fetch PC even
when imem is unready or the slot is full. The redirected target uses the
empty-slot bypass on its first ready cycle, preserving the existing
misprediction latency. Reset cancels buffered work. Flush only the slot's
valid bit; do not distribute recovery into its wide payload reset/enable.
A stored prediction is immutable through all waits and predictor updates;
EX compares against the prediction that actually advanced the fetch PC.
Keep all sixteen full-tag predictor entries, counter policy, row-local
event capture, target commit timing, and resolve-on-advancement rules.

must finish before this event, as enforced by the existing backend hold.
This instruction still retires once with its existing legal NOP result

No queued instruction may cause architectural side effects before issue;

All correctness and FPGA gates passed. The measured hypothesis regressed fitness: scored 2 KB CoreMark fell from 388.659115376458 to 211.905244438014 iterations/s (-45.48%), despite 4.25% fewer bracketed cycles, because median Fmax fell from 163.83 to 85.53 MHz.

Implemented the hypothesis in bench RTL only. The frontend now holds exactly one `if_id_t` tuple: PC, instruction, the prediction used to advance the fetch PC, and validity. An empty slot bypasses directly into ID. Fetch and issue have independent acceptance events, including capture during load-use/memory/divide waits, issue with an unready instruction bus, and atomic consume/refill. Register operands are still captured by the unchanged ID stage at issue.

`available` is the unflushed OR of slot occupancy and instruction-bus readiness. The hazard unit uses this availability and the oldest selected instruction's raw source fields. EX recovery cancels both transfers, invalidates the slot, substitutes a decoding NOP, and redirects regardless of instruction-bus readiness or occupancy. Only validity is reset/flushed; the 96 payload bits have an ordinary capture/refill enable with no reset or recovery input.

A legal FENCE.I uses the existing advancement-qualified EX recovery mechanism even when its saved prediction equals PC+4. This discards younger work after an older stalled memory operation completes and refetches PC+4. Its existing legal NOP result and single retirement are preserved. Decoder legality and ordinary FENCE are unchanged.

The sixteen full-tag predictor entries, counter policy, private row event capture, target commit timing, and advancement-only training remain unchanged. ID/EX control-versus-payload reset separation, EX/MEM, MEM/WB forwarding retention, real/ALTOPS arithmetic, the eight-edge divider, public ports, `nret: 1`, and channel-0 retirement wiring are unchanged.

## Implementation choices and scope

- Added two narrow unflushed source-address outputs to IF for hazard detection. Using the recovery-substituted ID instruction for these comparisons would indirectly put recovery into the slot's wide enable through `stall_if`; these outputs remove that path. ID still receives the prescribed NOP substitution.
- Kept the existing internal `stall`/`stall_if` names, now describing issue blocking. An empty fetch slot can fill while they are asserted.
- Inert payload can update on empty bypass or cancellation; validity alone determines whether it is retained work. Full occupied holds preserve the entire tuple.
- Gate sources and the incoming RTL were copied unchanged beneath the supplied TMPDIR. Generated artifacts stayed there. The delivered RTL and tests were checked byte-for-byte against the final gate inputs. Protected gate and benchmark sources were also checked unchanged. This notes file uses the explicitly requested current-directory location.

## Verification

- Required Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings.
- Unchanged pytest/cocotb suite with extended permitted tests: PASS, 9 pytest cases / 148 cocotb tests, including 27 real and 27 ALTOPS ALU tests, 43 pipeline tests, six frontend tests, and the exhaustive hazard truth table.
- Formal: PASS, 53 passed / 0 failed, including liveness, on the delivered RTL. Both local verification runs passed. No formal counterexample or RTL fix after a formal failure occurred (zero formal fix attempts).
- Unchanged `make cosim TARGET=bench`: PASS, selftest ISS and scored CoreMark validation.
- Additional unchanged ISS comparison under both bus stalls: PASS, 115 retirements each for seeds `0xDEADBEEF`, `0x16C0FFEE`, and `0xF37C4`.
- Canonical 6000-byte, `-O3`, ten-iteration CoreMark: PASS for incoming and delivered RTL with both bus stalls. Accepted start/stop markers, `oob=false`, and `Correct operation validated.` were required. CRCs: seed `8a02`, list `d4b0`, matrix `be52`, state `5e47`, final `5949`.
- Scored 2000-byte, `-O3`, ten-iteration CoreMark: PASS for both implementations. CRCs: `e9f5/e714/1fd7/8e3a/fcaf`.
- Synthesized slot audit: 97 source bits; all 96 payload bits are plain DFFE registers sharing one enable. No reset, EX PC, or EX saved-prediction input reaches that enable's combinational leaf cone.

The extended scoreboards account for every accepted fetch as issued, discarded, or still occupying the single slot. They check saved tuple stability on every occupied edge, prediction policy before/after commits, unique EX resolutions, ordered exactly-once RVFI, and physical read/store handshakes. Directed cases cover differing queued/live source fields, a register write after enqueue, divides, reset, full-slot recovery with imem unready, wrong-path stores/divides, ready-bus throughput, and instruction-memory changes at an older store's acceptance before FENCE.I recovery.

The three deterministic random pipeline runs recorded 55 queued issues with imem unready, 27 captures during load-use, five during memory holds, 26 during divide waits, three recovery discards, and 223 consume/refills. Capture categories can overlap. These are unit-test coverage counts, not CoreMark instrumentation. Ready-bus straight-line code retained consecutive retirements starting on cycle 2.

An initial test assertion incorrectly required every load-use wait to begin empty. It was corrected to require capture exactly when the slot is empty and retention when full. An initial direct `make fpga` invocation selected the default dual-retirement wrapper; subsequent invocations explicitly selected the unchanged single-retirement wrapper with `BENCH=fpga/core_bench_si.sv` and `NRET=1`. A preliminary FPGA run was stopped after the final hazard-source separation; its timing is excluded.

## Workload comparison

Both implementations ran each identical ELF with `--bench --istall --dstall --seed 3735928559` and a 50,000,000-cycle ceiling. Brackets below use accepted physical MMIO start/stop handshakes, excluding initialization and output. The final hazard-source separation preserved the complete benchmark output and these cycle counts.

The 6 KB UART size is the per-algorithm allocation, while the compiler command sets `TOTAL_DATA_SIZE=6000` and the canonical CRCs confirm the workload.

## FPGA measurement and concerns

The unchanged FPGA gate passed all three routed seeds for both designs. The incoming winner was rebuilt and measured live, reproducing the historical 388.66 result. The cycle savings do not compensate for the Fmax loss.

Median Fmax decreased 47.79%; LUT4 increased 2.37% and FF increased 3.16%. Canonical 6 KB cycles decreased 3.60%, but its separately calculated fitness decreased 45.84%. These calculations use the exact bracket lengths and median frequency in Hz.

All final critical paths originate in EX instruction opcode/funct3 bits used by FENCE.I detection and return through recovery/NOP substitution to ID. Seeds 1 and 2 terminate at ID/EX `rs1_val[14]` and `rs1_val[13]`; seed 3 terminates at ID/EX `ctrl.is_illegal`. This recovery-to-decode path is the measured timing concern; separating the slot payload enable did not remove the NOP-substitution data path required by the hypothesis.

title: Train the predictor from registered EX/MEM results
motivation:
Predictor history favors reducing update-path delay over adding accuracy:
the return stack saved only 0.17% of scored cycles, while associativity,
smaller tables, partial tags, and untagged direction training regressed.
The latest raw-event experiment, hyp-20260905-003-r9s2, still drove sixteen
private taken-outcome capture registers from the forwarded EX comparison;
that path limited all three seeds to a 125.47 MHz median. Changing the
classification boundary did not isolate the comparator from row fanout.

The existing EX/MEM bundle already registers the resolving instruction's
PC, architectural next PC, branch outcome, control-flow kind, and legality.
Reusing these results can move predictor classification, row selection,
target capture, and their fanout entirely behind that register boundary.
This differs from r9s2's direct per-row raw capture and from r6s1's added
tag-validation stage with alias forwarding. Saved incoming RTL matches
the current files byte-for-byte; its three routed limits are EX result
capture or ID/EX recovery, so a predictor timing gain is uncertain and
must be established by the full routed fitness product.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Source predictor training from the existing EX/MEM register rather than
live EX resolution. Introduce one registered training-valid token in
core.sv: reset clears it; every other edge assigns it the current
resolve_valid. Do not clock-enable or hold this token on pipeline stalls.
The existing resolve_valid remains the advancing-EX event, qualified by
in.valid, !stall, !div_wait, and !reset, and continues to qualify immediate
architectural recovery. Keep these live resolution signals available to
the pipeline checker independently of the delayed training interface.

Connect if_stage's training inputs to that token and the corresponding
EX/MEM fields: PC from ex_mem_w.pc, target from ex_mem_w.pc_next, branch
and jump flags from ex_mem_w.ctrl, taken from ex_mem_w.branch_taken, and
legal from !ex_mem_w.ctrl.is_illegal. Use the EX/MEM control bundle before
MEM-stage memory-alignment processing. The registered architectural next
PC is the exact target for legal jumps and taken branches, including
JALR's cleared low bit. Its value is irrelevant for NOT_TAKEN and
INVALIDATE commands, which must never write target storage. Preserve
EX's existing decoder and target-misalignment trap decisions.

For an instruction advancing at edge N, EX/MEM captures its results and
the token becomes valid at N. The unchanged private row-event registers
and indexed target-event register accept this registered feedback at
N+1; metadata and target commit together at N+2. This adds exactly one
training-visibility cycle to the current N+1 commit. At N+1, capture must
see the pre-edge EX/MEM payload even if a newer instruction advances on
that same edge. Consecutive advancing instructions can generate consecutive
valid tokens: sustain one training transaction per clock without a queue,
backpressure, table-state snapshots, or maintenance forwarding.

Use the independent token, not EX/MEM.valid or MEM acceptance, to identify
new training work. When EX/MEM holds for multiple data-bus stall cycles,
its older event is still accepted once and the token then clears; the
held instruction must not train repeatedly. Likewise, an EX divide wait
cannot replay a token or suppress previously captured work. A younger
redirect, imem stall, load-use bubble, or backend hold must not cancel or
pause older predictor events. Reset alone cancels the token and all
existing pending/table validity, preventing pre-reset publication.

Keep if_stage's sixteen PC[5:2] rows, full PC[31:6] tags, thirty target
bits, binary saturating counters, existing command encoding, row-local
commit logic, and target-write qualification unchanged. Legal jumps set
11; taken branches allocate 10 on a miss or increment a hit; not-taken
branches decrement only a hit and retain the target; non-controls and
traps invalidate only a matching entry. Fetch uses committed state with
the existing pre-edge semantics and no pending-event bypass. Preserve
exact accepted predicted_next_pc tracking and EX recovery for every
instruction, including stale non-controls, changing indirect targets,
and traps. Recovery still overrides imem backpressure immediately and
RVFI still reports the resolved architectural next PC.

The intended benefit is fewer live EX loads and a full register boundary
before predictor classification and fanout. Reuse EX/MEM payload registers
instead of adding another wide raw-event bank; mapped state can still
grow if previously unused EX/MEM fields become live. The unmeasured net
estimate is +4% fitness with low confidence. Local tag-to-counter paths
remain, the EX result/recovery path may remain critical, and extra cold
or rapidly changing branch misses can outweigh any frequency gain.
Inspect synthesized and routed capture cones to confirm row-event and
target-event D/enables now originate in registered EX/MEM results and
the token, without a live EX feedback bypass. Record all three timing
paths and LUT/FF counts; do not substitute source-level reasoning for
a measured Fmax improvement.

Run the unchanged lint, cocotb, formal, stalled cosim, and three-seed FPGA
gates. Measure exact iterations divided by accepted-marker bracketed
cycles times median Fmax using identical incoming/candidate ELFs and bus
schedules. History identifies 388.66 with a scored 2 KB image; report
that comparison separately from the required canonical 6 KB, ten-iteration,
-O3 run without changing the evaluator. Validate the latter's bounds,
both bus stalls, CRCs d4b0/be52/5e47, accepted start/stop markers, and
literal Correct operation validated. Preserve nret=1, external ports,
RVFI ordering and trap checks, all arithmetic and forwarding behavior,
and every protected contract file. This is solely a predictor-training
source and latency experiment.

title: Remove divide-bubble reset fanout from EX/MEM payload registers
motivation:
The winning r5s0 experiment improved fitness 4.61% by clearing ID/EX
controls and validity on bubbles while allowing inactive payloads to
capture normally. EX/MEM still clears its entire bundle on div_wait,
distributing decoded divide status and result readiness to wide data
registers even though zero controls already suppress their effects.

Saved incoming RTL in .tmp/load-use-r10s0/incoming matches the current
bench RTL byte-for-byte. Its mapped EX/MEM alu_result[25] register has
a reset cone combining external reset with divide-wait qualification.
Routed seeds 1 and 3 end at that register's D input through ALU operation
selection, at 6.10 and 5.93 ns; seed 2 instead limits recovery into
ID/EX.valid at 6.44 ns. This establishes wide divide-reset fanout and
timing-sensitive EX result capture, but does not establish that the
divide-reset cone itself is the present critical path.

Earlier ALU predecode, link-selection, and forwarding rewrites lost
frequency. The r10s0 profile also found only 61 immediately removable
false load-use bubbles in 4,215,262 scored cycles, alongside an RVFI
operand failure. Apply the successful control/payload separation to
the remaining EX/MEM divide-bubble boundary as one local timing bet.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split only the EX/MEM register updates in rtl/ex_stage.sv into disjoint
control/valid and payload groups. Preserve the control group's exact
priority: reset clears the entire ctrl field and valid; a dmem stall
holds them; otherwise div_wait clears the entire ctrl field and valid;
otherwise capture ctrl_with_trap and in.valid. Clear every control bit,
including reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_jump, and is_branch.

Keep deterministic reset-to-zero for every payload field. Outside reset,
hold payloads only when the existing stall input is asserted. On every
other edge capture the existing normal-advance expressions, including
while div_wait is high. Apply this to pc, alu_result, write_data, rd,
both source addresses and values, pc_next, branch_taken, branch_target,
and instr. In particular, alu_result still selects PC+4 for jumps and
the unchanged ALU output otherwise; the source-value fields still use
the accepted div_rs1_q/div_rs2_q snapshots for a divide. Do not add a
div_wait mask, clear, or hold to any payload data, reset, or enable cone.
Assign each field from exactly one sequential owner; remove the old
whole-struct assignments rather than overlapping them with field writes.

A divide-wait bubble may therefore contain nonzero instruction, address,
destination, and operand payloads, but ctrl=0 and valid=0 must make it

must remain zero, and the bubble must neither retire nor update registers.
Keep all existing downstream control qualification. Do not replace
complete control clearing with valid-only gating or change RVFI source
addresses or values. Inactive bus address/data may differ; accepted

implementation_notes:
# EX/MEM divide-bubble payload capture — r11s0

Implemented the hypothesis. Correctness gates passed; the timing bet regressed.
Candidate median Fmax is 148.06 MHz versus the saved incoming 163.83 MHz.
With identical bracketed cycles, fitness decreased 9.625831654764095%.

## Implementation

- Only `cores/bench/rtl/ex_stage.sv` changed in RTL. EX/MEM controls and valid
  have one sequential owner with the exact priority reset, memory hold,
  divide-wait clear, normal capture. All 22 control bits clear on a wait.
- All 272 payload bits retain deterministic zero reset and hold only on
  `stall`. Every other edge captures the original normal expressions,
  including divide waits. Jump PC+4 selection, accepted divide operand
  snapshots, metadata, and branch expressions are unchanged. No whole-struct
  assignment remains in EX/MEM, and no field has overlapping owners.
- `cores/bench/test/test_pipeline.py` replaces the two implementation-specific
  whole-zero divide-bubble checks with complete control/valid clearing and
  side-effect checks. A field-level oracle samples every normal expression
  before each edge and verifies reset, complete memory hold, and every
  unheld capture. It checks old snapshots on the launch edge and accepted
  snapshots on following wait edges.
- Bubble checks reject EX/MEM forwarding, memory requests, retirement and
  register writes. Directed in-place DIV/REM destinations match source

The saved `.tmp/load-use-r10s0/incoming/cores/bench/rtl/*.sv` was verified

## Synthesized register control cones

After Yosys `proc; opt`, every one of the 272 EX/MEM payload bits is owned
by a `$sdffe` with zero synchronous reset directly from `reset` and
active-low enable directly from `stall`; neither pin depends on `div_wait`.

are DFFR cells whose RESET pin connects directly to `cpu.reset`. They have
no physical enable pin; the memory hold is implemented in D feedback.
Shared/unused fields account for the difference from 272 source-level bits.

No RTL deviation from the hypothesis. Scratch staging isolated generated
formal outputs from the read-only shared framework; implementation notes
are at the requested worktree-root path. All tracked implementation edits

lesson: - 2026-09-06 hyp-20260905-001-r11s0 (regression, -9.63%): Extending ID/EX's control/payload split to EX/MEM removed `div_wait` from payload reset/enable cones but regressed median Fmax from 163.83 to 148.06 MHz with identical CoreMark cycles because ALU-result selection and forwarding/JALR target capture limited routed timing; wide reset fanout does not establish that reset removal will shorten the critical data path.

title: Move the complete multiply family into one shared MEM execution lane
motivation:
The incoming winner reaches 163.83 MHz, but its recorded routed limits
include ID/EX ALU control through result selection into EX/MEM in seeds
1 and 3; seed 2 is limited by recovery control. The structural r9s1
experiment moved only MULH/MULHU/MULHSU to MEM and regressed 18.10%:
retaining MUL in EX split the original shared multiplier into two
MULT36X36 cells, while fast-ALU selection and forwarding/JALR paths
remained limiting. It also moved no multiplication executed inside the
measured CoreMark bracket. This suggests testing a complete multiply
stage repartition that preserves sharing and removes every multiply
result from the fast EX selector. Unlike that earlier experiment, this
incurs a real dependency cost for timed MUL instructions, so a fitness
gain requires a measured clock improvement larger than the cycle cost.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Execute MUL, MULH, MULHU, and MULHSU together in one combinational
multiplier lane in MEM, using the existing EX/MEM registered,
post-forward rs1_val and rs2_val. EX forwards and captures multiply
operands; MEM performs multiplication and captures the final 32-bit
result into MEM/WB. Ordinary integer operations remain in EX. This is
one structural relocation of the entire multiplication resource, with
no added instruction stage, retirement channel, or predictor change.

Move all four real multiply result arms and their shared product
expressions out of the production EX ALU into rtl/mul_unit.sv. Preserve
the existing signed/signed, unsigned/unsigned, and signed/unsigned
arithmetic and low/high slice semantics, including the shared unsigned
product for MUL and MULHU. Keep every expression on the same registered
operand pair and in the same lane so synthesis can retain the incoming
design's sharing. Do not retain a separate EX MUL-low instance or add
another multiplier algorithm. Inspect the mapped design: the intended
resource result is one shared MULT36X36, rather than r9s1's two. Treat
sharing as something to verify, not a guaranteed inference from RTL.

Add a legal is_mul control bit in ID, covering all four multiply
operations. Reset and bubbles clear it with all other controls, while
backend holds retain it. EX still captures the exact instruction,
destination, operands, resolved next PC, and trap metadata. Its unused
multiply alu_result may be zero; this placeholder must never supply an
architectural result or override a correct forwarding source. In MEM,
select the lane result into MEM/WB.alu_result for is_mul and retain the
ordinary memory and nonmultiply paths for other instructions. WB and
RVFI then consume the registered final result through their current mux.

Generalize the existing late-producer interlock from mem_read to
mem_read OR is_mul. An immediately dependent instruction holds at fetch
and receives one ID/EX bubble on ready buses, then obtains the product
from MEM/WB forwarding. Retain the current nonzero-rd and BOTH RAW
fetched source-field comparisons; do not fold r10s0's failed operand-use
filtering into this experiment. Mask EX/MEM forwarding eligibility for
is_mul so the placeholder cannot be selected. Preserve MEM/WB forwarding
from retained payload even after its retirement-valid bit clears during
a memory hold. Do not add a combinational MEM-multiplier-to-EX bypass.

Independent multiplies can traverse EX and MEM on consecutive clocks
and retire one per clock. A multiply occupying MEM is not a data-bus
request and must advance when dmemReady is low. Actual older memory
requests retain the existing hold/drain priorities and exactly-once
side effects. Keep the divider's eight-edge handshake, accepted operand
snapshots, and retained-result behavior unchanged. A divide dependent
on a multiply uses the same late-producer interlock before launch.
Preserve EX recovery and predictor training timing, including recovery
of stale predictions on multiply instructions. Reset and wrong-path
bubbles must never leave an active multiply control on inert payload.

Relocate the multiply ALTOPS formulas with the operations:
MUL=(a+b)^0x5876063e, MULH=(a+b)^0xf6583fb7,
MULHU=(a+b)^0x949ce5e8, MULHSU=(a-b)^0xecfbe137, using 32-bit modular
arithmetic. Real and ALTOPS builds have identical stage availability
and dependency interlocks. Preserve every existing multiply test vector
and its exact expected value by exercising the new lane and integrated
retirement; changing the execution module must not reduce coverage.

Estimate an unmeasured four-percent fitness gain with low confidence.
Removing all multiply selection from EX and restoring a single physical
multiply resource may improve placement and fast execution timing, but
MEM multiplication, forwarding/JALR, recovery, or predictor maintenance
may become the limit. Immediate MUL dependencies can increase CoreMark
cycles enough to defeat any clock gain. Measure bracketed MUL counts,
immediate raw dependencies, and actual added interlock cycles under
identical ELFs and bus-ready seeds. Inspect all three routed paths and
confirm that multiplier operands originate in EX/MEM, its result first
reaches MEM/WB, and there is no live product path back into EX.

Compare exact iterations/bracketed_cycles times median_Fmax_Hz with the
incoming winner; success requires Fmax_new/Fmax_old > cycles_new/cycles_old.
History associates 388.66 with the scored 2 KB workload, so report that
like-for-like result separately from the required canonical 6 KB run.
Run unchanged lint, cocotb, formal including liveness, stalled ISS cosim,
and three-seed FPGA gates. Validate the canonical 6 KB, -O3, ten-iteration
workload with both bus stalls, d4b0/be52/5e47 CRCs, the literal Correct
operation validated., and accepted start/stop MMIO brackets. Preserve
nret=1, all external ports, channel-0 retirement order and RVFI operands,
decoder legality and traps, memory bounds, and every hard invariant.
Implementation is confined to cores/bench RTL and permitted unit tests.

implementation_notes:
Implemented the complete MEM multiply lane. Correctness gates pass, but the measured hypothesis regresses fitness: the scored 2 KB result is 349.627563 iterations/s versus the incoming 388.659115 (-10.042618%). The proposed +4% gain was an unmeasured, low-confidence estimate and was not achieved.

Changes made:

- Added `cores/bench/rtl/mul_unit.sv` with all four original real multiply expressions and result slices. MUL/MULHU share the unsigned product; MULH and MULHSU retain the original signed extensions and high-half semantics. All four original ALTOPS formulas moved with them.
- Removed every product expression and multiply result arm from the production EX ALU. Multiply opcodes now select its zero default.
- Added `ctrl_t.is_mul`, classified in ID only for valid, legal decoded multiplies. The existing control reset/flush and payload hold separation remains intact.
- MEM consumes the EX/MEM registered post-forward operand pair and operation, and captures the selected multiply result in MEM/WB.alu_result. WB and channel-0 RVFI use the existing registered-result mux.
- Generalized the historical `id_ex_mem_read` hazard input to `mem_read | is_mul`, preserving its name, every hazard equation, both raw fetched source-field comparisons, and the nonzero-rd requirement. Masked only multiply EX/MEM forwarding eligibility. Retained MEM/WB forwarding remains independent of retirement-valid.
- Kept the divider, EX advancement/recovery, predictor, decoder, external ports, nret=1, memory handling, and retirement order unchanged. No live MEM-product bypass, extra stage, multiplier algorithm, or EX MUL-low instance was added.

Tests preserve all prior assertions and vectors. The ALU test uses a temporary wrapper to exercise the unchanged integer/divider ALU and the relocated multiply lane together; all 185 boundary/random pairs per M operation and explicit expected results remain covered in real and ALTOPS builds. Integrated retirement also exercises all 740 multiply boundary/random vectors, the nine original explicit multiply expectations, and seven MUL vectors used while the divider is busy. Added coverage includes all four variants, immediate and one-gap consumers, both raw unused-source aliases, consecutive independent multiplication, repeated rd, x0, branches/JALR, store base/data, loads, multiply/divide chains, retained WB forwarding after valid clears, older memory holds, separate and simultaneous bus stalls, exactly-once markers, reset, illegal encodings, wrong-path multiplies, and stale prediction recovery with and without instruction-bus backpressure.

Added opt-in `test_mul_profile.py` to measure existing CoreMark ELFs without modifying the cosim driver. It generates a temporary C++ subclass that observes settled internal signals and retirement while the unchanged driver supplies instructions, memory, and its original bus-ready sequence. Its observed marker cycles match the uninstrumented binaries for every comparison below. A qualified-name filter and explicit executed-test count prevent an accidentally empty ALTOPS pipeline run; an initial unqualified filter was corrected before the final suite.

Local validation:

- Required `verilator --lint-only -Wall -Wno-MULTITOP -sv +incdir+cores/bench/rtl cores/bench/rtl/*.sv`: PASS without warnings. The same lint with `-DRISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS`: PASS without warnings.
- Final full pytest/cocotb suite: **10 passed, 1 skipped**. The skip is the opt-in CoreMark profiler when no ELFs are supplied; it was separately enabled and passed for both incoming and new RTL. The ALTOPS pipeline runner explicitly requires all eight new multiply tests to execute. Integer, divide, decode, predictor, and other existing tests still run in the normal suite.
- Local formal: **PASS on the first RTL attempt, 53 passed / 0 failed**, including `liveness_ch0`, instruction checks, reg, causal, unique, ill, and cover. Used unchanged `bash formal/run_all.sh` with `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=6`, which autodetected nret=1 and selected the unchanged single-issue wrapper/configuration.
- Unchanged `tools.eval.cosim`: PASS, two ELFs (selftest and scored 2 KB CoreMark).
- Additional stalled ISS comparison through the unchanged `run_cosim.compare`: selftest passed at bus seeds 0xdeadbeef, 1, and 2 (115 retirements each). A generated arithmetic ELF covering all 185 pairs for each of the eight M operations plus immediate consumers passed at the same three bus seeds (3,701 retirements each).

title: Prevalidate sequential and direct-target predictions in decode
motivation:
Recent predictor changes have repeatedly lost frequency: untagged direction
training, raw-event capture, and EX/MEM-sourced training regressed by 33.64%,
23.41%, and 12.29%. Accuracy additions have offered little cycle headroom;
the return stack saved only 0.17% of the historically scored cycles. The
next predictor experiment should shorten prediction validation itself.

The current RTL matches the saved incoming winner in the r8s2 evidence
byte-for-byte. Its seed-2 critical path starts at ID/EX predicted_next_pc[3]
and ends at ID/EX valid RESET, taking 6.44 ns at 155.33 MHz. EX currently
selects a full actual_next_pc before comparing it with the prediction.
Sequential and direct-target equality need no forwarded register operands,
so both comparisons can finish before EX. The earlier r7s1 address-retiming
experiment retained the late equality and changed ALU/AUIPC routing; this
proposal registers only prediction-match bits and leaves those datapaths
intact. Seeds 1 and 3 were ALU-result limited, making confidence low.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Prevalidate the two operand-independent possible successors in ID and
carry their exact equality results with the instruction. Add two one-bit
id_ex_t payload fields, prediction_matches_seq and prediction_matches_direct.
Compute them in id_stage from the same IF bundle and decoded immediate
that the existing ID/EX payload captures:
  prediction_matches_seq = (in.predicted_next_pc == seq_pc);
  prediction_matches_direct = (in.predicted_next_pc == direct_pc);
Here seq_pc is the 32-bit result of in.pc + 32'd4, and direct_pc is the
32-bit result of in.pc + imm. Explicitly truncate both sums modulo 2^32
before equality. Compare all 32 bits, including target alignment bits.
These are exact destination comparisons, not predicted-direction hints
or truncated target signatures. Retain the full predicted_next_pc field.

Register both bits at the existing ID/EX boundary with exactly the winning
payload discipline: deterministic zero on reset, retain on the existing
backend stall, otherwise capture even if a flush makes the payload inert.
Flush still clears every ctrl bit and valid independently. Give each new
field one sequential owner. Do not add the recovery or load-use signals
to these payload fields' reset or enable cones. Never recompute a held
instruction's match bits from live fetch, predictor state, or operands.

Replace only EX's final prediction-correctness calculation. Start with
prediction_correct = in.prediction_matches_seq. If ctrl_with_trap is legal,
a jump selects in.prediction_matches_direct for JAL, or the full equality
of in.predicted_next_pc and the existing forwarded, bit-zero-cleared
jump_target for JALR. Otherwise a taken conditional branch selects
in.prediction_matches_direct; an untaken branch or non-control retains
in.prediction_matches_seq. A decoder or target-alignment trap always uses
the sequential match, following the existing PC+4 trap recovery policy.
Keep redirect = resolve_valid && !prediction_correct. Compute the JALR
equality against jump_target directly, in parallel with the final Boolean
selection, rather than comparing against the selected actual_next_pc.

Leave actual_next_pc generation unchanged for redirect_target and EX/MEM
pc_next, and retain the existing branch comparator, JALR forwarding,
alignment checks, link writes, and EX predictor feedback. Retain the
original resolve_valid qualification by in.valid, !stall, !div_wait, and
!reset. This must be Boolean-equivalent to the original full destination
mismatch for every advancing instruction. In particular, a taken transfer
whose destination equals PC+4 must not spuriously redirect; a stale target
on an ordinary instruction or completed divide must still recover; and a
changing JALR target must recover even when both predictions are taken.
Only operand-dependent JALR destination comparison remains in EX.

This is a predictor-validation retiming experiment, with no additional
pipeline stage, early ID redirect, or change in prediction policy. Keep
the sixteen full-tag target rows, binary counters, private pending events,
training source and latency, atomic target/tag commit, and reset handling
exactly as they are. Preserve accepted-prediction tracking, instruction
bus recovery priority, load-use bubbles, memory holds, and divide waits.
No changes to arithmetic selection, AUIPC, forwarding, or the hazard unit
are part of this hypothesis. The two ID comparison sums are local wires;
do not add registered PC+4/PC+imm buses or route them into the ALU.

The unmeasured estimate is a 3% fitness improvement through higher median
Fmax, with identical cycles for identical ELF and ready schedules. Risks
include the existing BTB lookup plus a comparison becoming an ID critical
path, instruction/immediate decode plus addition and equality limiting ID,
duplicated adders increasing routing cost, and unchanged ALU, JALR, or
predictor-training paths remaining limiting. Inspect synthesized and all
three routed netlists to confirm that the new match bits survive as flops
and sequential/direct recovery selects registered one-bit results rather
than retaining the original selected-next-PC equality. Report LUT/FF cost
and all three critical paths; source-level shortening is not a result.

Run the unchanged lint, cocotb, formal, stalled cosim, and three-seed FPGA
gates. Preserve the pipeline oracle's independent assertion that redirect
equals actual_next_pc != the prediction recorded at fetch acceptance;
do not replace its expected value with the new RTL match bits. Compare
incoming and candidate prediction decisions, recovery cycles, accepted
memory transactions, and RVFI retirements under identical ready schedules.
Require identical bracketed CoreMark cycles, not merely matching CRCs.
Compute fitness using exact iterations/bracketed_cycles times median Fmax.
Validate the required canonical 6 KB, ten-iteration, -O3 run with both
bus stalls, bounded accesses, accepted start/stop markers, CRCs
d4b0/be52/5e47, and the literal Correct operation validated. History assigns
388.66 to a scored 2 KB image; report that historical comparison separately
from like-for-like canonical 6 KB throughput without changing the evaluator.
Preserve nret=1, external ports, RVFI ordering and trap checks, decoder
legality, real/ALTOPS arithmetic, and every protected contract file.

implementation_notes:
Implemented the decode prediction-validation retiming exactly as proposed. Correctness gates pass, but the measured hypothesis is a performance regression: median routed Fmax falls from 163.83 MHz to 56.61 MHz (65.445889% lower) with identical benchmark cycles.

Changes are limited to three RTL files and three test files, plus these requested notes. `id_ex_t` retains the full prediction and adds two one-bit payload fields. ID computes local 32-bit PC+4 and PC+imm sums and compares all 32 prediction bits. Each match bit has one sequential owner: reset to zero, hold only on the existing backend stall, otherwise capture independently of flush. The existing control/valid flush priority is unchanged. EX selects the registered sequential/direct match or the independent equality against the existing forwarded, bit-zero-cleared JALR jump_target. Trap recovery selects the sequential match. resolve_valid, actual_next_pc, redirect_target, EX/MEM pc_next, arithmetic, forwarding, hazards, predictor policy/state/training, and nret=1 are unchanged. All eleven other RTL files are byte-identical to the incoming snapshot. No registered address buses or pipeline stages were added.

Tests now decode immediates independently from instruction encodings, unpack both match fields, and check payload capture on every advancing pipeline edge. ID tests cover every reset/flush/hold combination with changing inputs, positive/negative B/J offsets, modulo-2^32 wraparound, exact matches, and a mismatch in each of the 32 target bits. Pipeline coverage includes PC+4 transfers, taken/untaken misaligned branches, stale ordinary/trapping/divide predictions, EX/MEM and MEM/WB forwarded changing JALR targets, link/operand values, memory/divide holds, predictor commits during holds, instruction-stalled recovery, reset, strict RVFI order/PC chaining, and wrong-path store/retirement exclusion. The original assertion `redirect == (actual != accepted_prediction)` and predictor-training oracle remain independent of the new match bits.

Added `test_prediction_equivalence.py` to capture/compare normalized incoming and candidate observations under identical cycle-driven ready schedules. The actual comparison passed for 11 scenarios, 365 cycles and 173 retirements, including every fetch prediction/acceptance, resolution/recovery cycle, accepted memory transaction, downstream bundle and complete RVFI record. Only the differently sized internal ID bundle and its derived input-expectation dictionary are excluded. Set PREDICTION_CAPTURE_TRACE to capture an incoming trace and PREDICTION_REFERENCE_TRACE to compare a candidate trace. Normal unit-test execution still exercises the independent pipeline assertions without these optional files.

Local validation completed using isolated scratch copies under `.tmp/prediction-validation/{incoming,candidate}`. Protected scripts, wrappers, benchmark sources, constraints and evaluator were copied unchanged; their generated outputs stay in scratch. No protected worktree files or other cores were changed.

- Exact requested Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings or errors.
- Unchanged `make test TARGET=bench`: PASS, all 10 pytest runners, including real and ALTOPS arithmetic, both ID tests and all 39 pipeline tests.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=6 bash formal/run_all.sh`: PASS on the first RTL attempt, 53 passed / 0 failed; automatically selected wrapper_si.sv/checks_si.cfg. No formal counterexample or RTL fix retries. formal-deep was not needed because arithmetic is unchanged.
- Unchanged `python -m tools.eval.cosim . bench`: PASS, selftest and stalled 2 KB CoreMark. Additional selftest runs with both stalls and ready seeds 1, 2 and 3 each matched the unchanged Python ISS for all 115 retirements; incoming/candidate full RVFI records, including cycle numbers, were identical.
- Unchanged `make fpga TARGET=bench NRET=1 BENCH=fpga/core_bench_si.sv`: PASS for incoming and candidate; all three seeds routed successfully. Explicit NRET/BENCH select the existing single-retirement contract. An initial incoming build omitted NRET and failed to compile channel-1 references; it was rerun with NRET=1, with no source changes.

The optimized pre-mapping netlists confirm that the incoming full predicted-PC comparison consumes actual_next_pc, while the candidate's only EX prediction comparator is a 32-bit equality against jump_target. Actual-next-PC selection still feeds recovery and retirement data. The mapped synthesis netlist AND all three routed netlists retain separate DFFRE cells for sequential/direct matches (`cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_96` and `_97`). Their clock, reset and enable connections equal those of the retained prediction payload; the valid flop has the separate flush reset. Sequential/direct Q values reach that recovery reset through two/three LUT cells respectively, rather than a selected-next-PC bus equality. Placement of the two match flops is:

| Seed | Sequential match | Direct match |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | X25Y20/DFF3 | X25Y20/DFF2 |
| 2 | X22Y5/DFF4 | X24Y10/DFF0 |
| 3 | X14Y3/DFF5 | X17Y26/DFF4 |

The new critical paths reveal the concern that dominates this implementation: EX/MEM destination-register forwarding selection propagates through JALR target/recovery logic, the existing IF instruction-to-NOP flush, immediate decoding, the local ID direct sum, and the direct-match flop's DATA input. Keeping recovery out of the new flop reset/enable cones does not remove this data path. It is sensitized structurally even though a flush makes the captured payload inert. The experiment therefore successfully retimes EX validation but extends recovery-to-decode payload capture enough to lose frequency. No attempt was made to change the specified IF-bundle capture discipline or other datapaths to hide this result.

title: Align M-extension operation codes for shallow ALU class selection
motivation:
The saved winner in .tmp/thermometer-r6s0/baseline/cores/bench/rtl
matches the current bench RTL byte for byte. Its routed seeds 1 and 3
launch from ID/EX alu_op[4] and alu_op[2] and end at EX/MEM
alu_result[25], taking 6.10 and 5.93 ns. The saved incoming reports in
.tmp/load-use-r10s0 show encoded operation selection passing through
seven mapped combinational cells. Seed 2 instead limits recovery into
ID/EX.valid at 6.44 ns. This motivates a local operation-encoding and
result-selection experiment, with unchanged instruction timing.

LESSONS.md and the micro_opt log entries were reviewed. Full registered
one-hot ALU selection in r2s0, a registered multiply-high class bit in
r7s0, and link-result folding in r9s0 all regressed. The proposed change
uses the existing five control bits and an aligned M-extension encoding;
the reviewed history contains no such encoding experiment. The current
MUL family occupies 11 through 14 and DIV/REM straddles 15 through 18,
making family membership irregular. Aligning both four-operation groups
can simplify their selection and the divide interlock without extra
predecode registers or changes to arithmetic latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Recode only the eight internal M-extension operation constants in
core_pkg.sv. Keep all integer operations ADD through LUI at 0 through
10, ALU_ADD=0 for cleared controls, and the five-bit ctrl.alu_op width.
Use this exact mapping, matching RV32M funct3 in the three low bits:
  MUL=16, MULH=17, MULHSU=18, MULHU=19,
  DIV=20, DIVU=21, REM=22, REMU=23.
Thus op[4:2]==3'b100 selects multiplication and 3'b101 selects
division/remainder. Codes 11 through 15 and 24 through 31 are unused
and must return zero without launching the divider. The instruction
decoder already assigns symbolic constants inside validated matches;
retain those matches, all other controls, and default illegality.

Factor the combinational ALU result into three exclusive contributions.
Compute integer_result with a case on op[3:0], keeping the existing
eleven integer expressions at codes 0 through 10 and default zero.
Compute multiply_result with a case on op[1:0]: 00 selects MUL low,
01 selects MULH, 10 selects MULHSU, and 11 selects MULHU. Preserve the
existing mul_ss, mul_su, and mul_uu expressions, widths, signedness,
and slices. Combine the results with parallel masked terms:
  out = ({32{!op[4]}} & integer_result)
      | ({32{op[4:2] == 3'b100}} & multiply_result)
      | ({32{(op[4:2] == 3'b101) && div_result_valid}} & div_result).
This replaces the irregular full-op result case with local suboperation
selection and shallow family qualification. Do not repeat five-bit
M-operation equality tests inside these family-qualified result paths.
Keep fully defined defaults; introduce no X values or synthesis-only
behavior to simplify unsupported operation codes.

Use the same exact three-bit DIV/REM class comparison in ex_stage.is_div
and div_unit.legal_op. Preserve EX's in.valid and !is_illegal qualifiers
and every request/result-ready/reset/stall condition. In the real
divider, signed_op may be legal_op && !op[0], and rem_op may be
legal_op && op[1]. Preserve req_ready behavior even when an invalid
operation is offered; only acceptance is legal-op qualified. Leave the
restoring datapath, accepting edge plus seven processing edges, saved
operands, corner cases, retained-result handshake, and controller exact.
This class simplification is part of the same encoding experiment.

In RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, the multiply suboperation selection must return
the original instruction-specific formulas: MUL add-XOR 5876063e,

newly encoded symbolic constants and the same eight-edge controller.
In particular, MULHSU and MULHU must not be swapped when adopting
funct3 order. Both arithmetic builds must implement identical control
classification and timing.

title: Rebuild the integer register file as replicated distributed RAM
motivation:
The current register file resets every data word synchronously, tying its
31 writable architectural registers to resettable storage and wide read
selection. Reorganizing that storage can remove about 992 data flip-flops
and replace their reset behavior with 31 useful validity bits, reducing
placement and routing pressure without adding instruction latency.

The structural history includes unsuccessful forwarding retiming
(hyp-20260905-002-r8s1), a fall-through fetch slot (r10s1), and relocation
of multiplication to MEM (r11s1). The latter raised 6 KB CoreMark cycles
1.48% and reduced median Fmax to 148.61 MHz. The register-file experiment
hyp-20260905-001-r1s0 changed read selection while retaining the original
storage and achieved only 0.54% fitness improvement. No logged hypothesis
has replaced the register-file storage with replicated distributed RAM.

This is a structural storage and reset reorganization. The installed
Gowin lutrams.txt describes synchronous-write, asynchronous-read 16x4
memories, and lutrams_map.v maps them to RAM16SDP primitives. The protected
synthesis script enables their inference. The incoming winner's measured
critical paths include ALU result selection and recovery, so a timing
improvement from lower routing pressure is a hypothesis, not evidence
that the register-file read port is currently the bottleneck.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement the 32x32, two-read/one-write integer register file using two
identical data copies, one per asynchronous read port. Organize each copy
as two 16x32 banks selected by address bit 4, with bits 3:0 addressing a
bank. Broadcast each accepted nonzero-register write to the corresponding
bank in both copies. Use synthesizable behavioral memory arrays with
distributed-RAM inference attributes; their clocked processes contain
writes only, with no data-array reset loop, scrub sequence, or initial
contents requirement. This organization is intended to map to roughly
32 RAM16SDP4 cells before optimization. Do not instantiate vendor-only
simulation black boxes or introduce different formal/simulation hardware.

Add a shared written-since-reset bitmap. A synchronous reset clears the
bitmap and suppresses physical writes on that edge. A non-reset write to
x1..x31 writes both copies and sets its bitmap bit on the same edge. Leave
x0 permanently invalid and unwritable. Reads select zero for x0, then the
existing live write-first bypass on a matching nonzero address, then the
selected bank's data if its bitmap bit is set, otherwise zero. In
particular, bypass takes priority over an unset bitmap bit. Preserve the
existing combinational bypass even while reset is asserted: reset wins
at the storage edge, but does not itself gate the live read mux. When
bypass is removed after a reset edge, every unwritten register reads zero.
Uninitialized or pre-reset RAM contents must never affect a visible read.

Keep reg_file's ports, synchronous write/reset semantics, two independent
zero-cycle reads, x0 behavior, and same-cycle WB visibility exact. Keep
instruction stages, hazards, forwarding, arithmetic, predictor, bus
acceptance, retirement, and nret=1 unchanged. This hypothesis adds no
instruction bubbles or resource scheduling changes. For identical
instruction images and bus-ready schedules, require identical RVFI
records and retirement cycles, accepted memory transactions, and timed
CoreMark cycles before assessing frequency.

implementation_notes:
Implemented the replicated distributed-RAM register file. All required local correctness gates pass, and the storage transformation is confirmed in synthesis and all three routed netlists. The measured result is nevertheless a fitness regression: median Fmax decreases from 163.83 MHz to 153.99 MHz, or 6.0062259659403%, with identical instruction timing and CoreMark cycles. The unmeasured 4% improvement estimate is not supported by this run.

Only `cores/bench/rtl/reg_file.sv`, `cores/bench/test/test_reg_file.py`, and `cores/bench/test/test_pipeline.py` changed, plus these requested notes. Every other RTL file is byte-identical to the incoming HEAD, `49caed5`. The pipeline, arithmetic, hazards, forwarding, predictor, bus interface, retirement rules, and `nret: 1` remain unchanged. No protected evaluator, wrapper, benchmark source, constraint, Makefile, or other core was edited.

The register file now contains four behavioral 16x32 arrays with `ram_style = "distributed"`: low/high banks for each independent asynchronous read port. Both copies receive the same accepted write address, data, clock, and bank enable. Their clocked process performs writes only; there is no RAM reset, initialization, scrub, vendor-only simulation primitive, or formal-specific implementation. A write is physically accepted only when `!reset && w_en && w_addr != 0`.

The shared written-since-reset bitmap has 31 generated sticky bits and a constant-zero x0 bit. The explicit per-register enables ensure exactly 31 validity flip-flops; an initial indexed bitmap assignment synthesized an unnecessary 32nd bit and extra selection logic, so it was replaced before final validation. Reset clears these bits synchronously. Read priority remains x0, matching live write bypass, valid bank data, then zero. In particular, bypass is independent of reset and overrides an unset validity bit; removing bypass after a reset edge immediately exposes zero without another edge.

The original register-file assertions remain. Their clock helpers now wait for simulator evaluation before withdrawing writes or reset. Added tests use an independent flat 32-register architectural scoreboard, all 1,024 read-address pairs, distinct patterns in every writable register, both banks and both ports, same-address reads, consecutive overwrites, disabled and zero-valued writes, randomized accesses, attempted x0 writes, dirty and repeated resets, and reset plus live bypass before/after the edge and after bypass removal. Tests observe public read data and never inspect RAM initialization.

The pipeline harness now checks both live ID register operands against a flat architectural scoreboard on every cycle, including stalls and restart. New integrated programs exercise x15/x16 dependencies, WB-to-ID bypass on either or both ports, WB writes during dmem and divide holds, load-use stalls, recovery, accepted stores, and dirty reset while a WB write is offered. After restart, every writable register is read through both EX operand ports before rewriting; RVFI must report zero operands, ordered retirement, and the original retirement cycles. The unchanged ISS, complete RVFI comparator, predictor oracle, payload/hold assertions, and divider assertions also check these programs.

title: XOR-folded PC indexing for the existing tagged target predictor
motivation:
The current sixteen-entry predictor places every instruction at the same
offset within a 64-byte block in the same row, because it indexes only
PC[5:2]. Recurring branches and jumps can therefore evict each other's
targets and direction history even when other rows are unused. The log
records 80,662 recoveries in 4,215,262 bracketed cycles for the winner's
historical scored workload, and 550,409 in 30,822,790 cycles for its
separate canonical 6 KB run. These totals include direction and changing
target misses; they are not measurements of recoverable index conflicts.

Prior attempts make the timing budget especially important. Two-way
prediction at unchanged capacity regressed 7.32% with essentially
unchanged cycles, and an eight-entry table regressed 8.60%. Untagged
direction training and later training stages also lost substantial Fmax.
No prior experiment in this log tests folded PC indexing. Changing only
the placement function is a small, untested way to reduce systematic
conflicts while retaining the winner's lookup and maintenance structure.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the index function in the existing sixteen-row direct-mapped
target predictor with index(PC) = PC[5:2] XOR PC[9:6]. This is the sole
architectural change. Use the identical four-bit function for fetch
lookup, resolving-event row selection, and the captured target-write
index. Retain the complete PC[31:6] tag, thirty-bit aligned target,
two-bit saturating counter, and all sixteen entries.

The unchanged tag remains sufficient for exact instruction identity:
for an aligned PC, PC[9:6] is contained in the tag, and PC[5:2] can be
recovered as index XOR tag[3:0]. Consequently two different aligned

title: Remove false load-use bubbles with exact late RVFI operand forwarding
motivation:
The current interlock compares a load destination against both raw fetched
instruction fields, including immediate bits that are not execution sources.
This creates avoidable bubbles after loads. The earlier micro_opt attempt
hyp-20260905-001-r10s0 suppressed these comparisons but failed reg_ch0:
EX/MEM forwarding supplied a load address for an unused reported operand.
That experiment did not establish the performance of a correct implementation.

The fixed ISS snapshots BOTH raw source fields for every instruction, and
run_cosim.py compares both addresses and values unconditionally. Zeroing unused
fields would therefore violate the existing evaluation contract. A small late
operand-reporting bypass can preserve these exact observations while removing
execution stalls. Recent ALU recoding and register-file remapping lost Fmax
with unchanged cycles; this experiment instead targets a concrete cycle cost.
