hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement one coherent micro-optimization: interlock only on execution sources,
and complete unused raw RVFI operand dependencies at the MEM/WB capture edge.
Keep raw register-file addresses, ID/EX source addresses and snapshots, and
both externally reported RVFI source addresses exactly as in the winner.

Add if_id_opcode to hazard_unit, wired from if_id_w.instr[6:0], and decode
source use in parallel with its existing five-bit equality comparisons.
Default uses_rs1=uses_rs2=1, preserving conservative behavior for SYSTEM and
unrecognized opcodes. For LOAD 0x03, OP-IMM 0x13 and JALR 0x67, use rs1 only.
For LUI 0x37, AUIPC 0x17, JAL 0x6f and MISC-MEM 0x0f, use neither source.
OP 0x33, STORE 0x23 and BRANCH 0x63 retain both, including every RV32M op.
This is instruction-format classification, not a legality decoder: reserved
encodings still follow the unchanged decoder and trap checks.

Set load_use_hazard to id_ex_mem_read && id_ex_rd!=0 &&
((uses_rs1 && id_ex_rd==if_id_rs1) ||
 (uses_rs2 && id_ex_rd==if_id_rs2)). Preserve every other hazard equation
and priority, including real load-use bubbles, backend holds, redirects,
instruction-bus stalls, and the winning ID/EX control/payload split.

Exclude loads from the existing EX/MEM forwarding eligibility in core.sv:
ex_mem_w.ctrl.reg_write && !ex_mem_w.ctrl.mem_read. The EX/MEM value for a
load is an address and must never masquerade as its register result. Keep
EX/MEM priority for other writers, existing MEM/WB forwarding, and x0 rules.
Real load consumers still interlock; a newly unstalled unused raw alias may
temporarily carry its older register snapshot, which cannot affect execution.
This exclusion also matters for a misaligned load that ultimately traps and
writes no register: its address must not contaminate the following trace.

Feed mem_stage a reporting-bypass tuple from the CURRENT registered MEM/WB
bundle: eligible = ctrl.mem_read && ctrl.reg_write && rd!=0, address = rd,
data = wb_w_data. Do not qualify eligible with MEM/WB.valid or wb_w_en.
MEM/WB deliberately retains its data and controls after clearing valid during
a data-memory hold, and that retained older load remains the right source.
The trap-adjusted ctrl.reg_write already excludes misaligned loads.

On each ordinary MEM/WB capture, independently set rs1_val and rs2_val to
the bypass data when eligible and the corresponding raw EX/MEM source
address equals the bypass address; otherwise preserve in.rs1_val/in.rs2_val.
Keep reset and hold_wb behavior unchanged. This comparison need not decode
source use again: for a real source the older value agrees with the existing
forwarded operand; for an unused alias it supplies the previously missing
load result. The source is strictly older in this in-order pipeline and is
sampled before the consumer's own write, including rd/source aliases.
The feedback crosses the existing MEM/WB register, so it introduces no
combinational loop, extra retirement stage, or combinational dmem-to-EX path.
Apply the bypass only to stored RVFI operand values, never to store data,
branch inputs, ALU operands, memory addresses, or architectural write data.

Example: LW x5,0(x1); ADDI x6,x2,5 has a false rs2 match because the immediate
encodes raw rs2=5. Allow ADDI to advance without a load-use bubble, compute
x6 from x2 and its immediate, and capture the preceding load's completed WB
result as ADDI's raw RVFI rs2_rdata. If that load traps, preserve x5's older
value instead. LW x5,0(x1); ADDI x6,x5,5 must still take the real rs1 bubble.

Estimate an unmeasured one-percent fitness gain from fewer bracketed cycles.
Confidence is low: removable matches have not been profiled, source-use
gating adds interlock logic, and the new reporting bypass is real hardware.
The FPGA wrapper retains RVFI fanout, so its LUT, routing and Fmax costs must
be measured rather than assumed to disappear. Count incoming false matches
separately from immediately removable bubbles, excluding overlaps with
imem stalls, redirects, dmem holds and divide waits. Compare actual cycles;

title: Register integer and multiply results separately before final selection
motivation:
The incoming winner's saved routed reports, reproduced in the r12s1
experiment, put ID/EX alu_op-to-EX/MEM alu_result selection on the
critical path in seeds 1 and 3: 6.10 ns and 5.93 ns. Seed 2 instead
limits on prediction recovery into ID/EX validity at 6.44 ns. These
are measured paths of the incoming design, not an assumption that
multiplier arithmetic itself limits frequency.

Structural attempts r9s1 and r11s1 moved multiplication into MEM and
regressed fitness. The latter preserved one MULT36X36, but added 1.48%
to canonical 6 KB CoreMark cycles and reduced median Fmax to 148.61 MHz.
The r12s1 distributed-RAM register file saved area without improving
the limiting EX and predictor paths. A different structural cut is to
move result-family selection across the existing EX/MEM boundary while
retaining EX computation and immediate dependent-instruction forwarding.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the single preselected EX/MEM execution-result register with
two parallel 32-bit result banks and one registered multiply-family
bit. One bank holds the existing non-multiply result, including integer
ALU work, effective addresses, completed DIV/REM, and JAL/JALR PC+4.
The other holds the selected MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU result. Both banks
capture at the existing EX/MEM edge from the same forwarded operands.
This is a relocation of the final result-family mux across a register
boundary; the instruction pipeline gains no stage or scheduling bubble.

In alu.sv, expose separate nonmul_result and multiply_result outputs.
The non-multiply case retains existing integer and divider expressions
and defined default-zero behavior, with no multiply contribution. The
multiply candidate contains the complete existing multiply family in
EX, using the original product expressions, widths, signedness, and
high/low slices. Select its suboperation with the current op[1:0]
mapping: 11=MUL, 00=MULH, 01=MULHU, 10=MULHSU. This candidate may have
a defined speculative value on non-multiply instructions; do not put
a five-bit multiply-family enable back on its wide capture data path.
Qualify architectural use with the separate family bit, captured from
a valid, legal decoded multiply. Keep operation encodings unchanged.
Preserve alu.out's existing standalone interface and full operation
semantics by selecting from the same candidate outputs. The core uses
the candidates directly, so that compatibility mux must synthesize
away from the core's EX/MEM capture cones.

Keep the ordinary bank as ex_mem_t.alu_result and add multiply_result
and result_is_mul fields. Apply the existing EX/MEM register discipline
to every new field: deterministic reset, complete hold on a data-memory
stall, complete zero bubble on div_wait, otherwise capture together
with destination, controls, operands, instruction, and PC metadata.
Keep JAL/JALR link selection on the ordinary bank and preserve the
divider's eight-edge controller, retained result handshake, and saved
post-forward operands. Both arithmetic builds must use this same
register and forwarding organization; ALTOPS retains every original
operation-specific formula and constant.

Supply both registered banks and result_is_mul to EX forwarding. Keep
forward_unit's dependency tests and EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB priority. For
each operand, combine source selection and family selection in one
parallel mux: original ID/EX operand; MEM/WB write data; EX/MEM ordinary
bank when the EX/MEM source wins and result_is_mul is clear; or EX/MEM
multiply bank when that source wins and result_is_mul is set. Use
mutually exclusive masks, avoiding a standalone family mux followed
serially by the old operand mux. Only registered result banks feed
this bypass; no live multiply output can bypass its EX/MEM register.
Preserve x0 handling, the existing raw-source/RVFI convention, and
MEM/WB forwarding-data retention during memory holds.

In MEM, use the ordinary bank directly for effective-address, alignment,
and memory-port logic. Select the architectural non-load result from
the two registered banks only when capturing MEM/WB. WB and RVFI keep
their current final registered result path. A MUL immediately followed
by an ALU operation, another MUL, a branch, JALR, or a store must use
the product at the same edge as today, with no multiply-use interlock.
Maintain the existing load-use interlock, accepted memory transactions,
bus hold behavior, predictor policy and training edges, recovery,
instruction legality, trap handling, and channel-0 retirement order.
Keep nret=1 and the entire core port set unchanged.

The unmeasured estimate is a 4% fitness improvement through Fmax at
unchanged instruction timing, with low confidence. The added bank,

`alu.sv` now exposes independent `nonmul_result` and `multiply_result` candidates. Integer operations, effective-address sums, and the retained divider result feed the ordinary candidate; multiply operations produce zero there. title: Validate sequential predictions from unflushed IF state
motivation:
Preserve the winner's prediction accuracy and target-table organization
while shortening prediction recovery. The r8s2 and r12s1 implementation
notes reproduce an incoming seed-2 critical path from registered
predicted_next_pc[3] to ID/EX valid.RESET; the other two incoming seeds
are limited by ALU result selection. Predictor capacity, associativity,
return prediction, partial tags, and XOR indexing have already regressed.
These results favor a small change to recovery timing with unchanged
prediction policy rather than assuming substantial residual cycle savings.

The related r11s2 experiment regressed 65.45% because prevalidating a
direct target in ID put recovery, IF NOP substitution, immediate decoding,
a 32-bit addition, and equality on one register-to-register path. That
result does not separately measure sequential-only validation from raw
fetch state. PC+4 prediction correctness needs neither instruction bits
nor an immediate, so it can cross the existing ID/EX boundary without
introducing that measured dependency.

hypothesis.motivation:
Preserve the winner's prediction accuracy and target-table organization
while shortening prediction recovery. The r8s2 and r12s1 implementation
notes reproduce an incoming seed-2 critical path from registered
predicted_next_pc[3] to ID/EX valid.RESET; the other two incoming seeds
are limited by ALU result selection. Predictor capacity, associativity,
return prediction, partial tags, and XOR indexing have already regressed.
These results favor a small change to recovery timing with unchanged
prediction policy rather than assuming substantial residual cycle savings.

The related r11s2 experiment regressed 65.45% because prevalidating a
direct target in ID put recovery, IF NOP substitution, immediate decoding,
a 32-bit addition, and equality on one register-to-register path. That
result does not separately measure sequential-only validation from raw
fetch state. PC+4 prediction correctness needs neither instruction bits
nor an immediate, so it can cross the existing ID/EX boundary without
introducing that measured dependency.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add exactly one prediction metadata bit, prediction_matches_seq, to the
combinational IF bundle and the existing ID/EX payload. In if_stage,
compute seq_pc = pc + 32'd4 with 32-bit wraparound, and define the bit
as the exact equality predicted_next_pc == seq_pc. Compute it solely
from the local, unflushed PC and committed predictor lookup. Reuse the
existing PC+4 expression. An equivalent implementation is true on the
sequential selection and a full 32-bit target-versus-seq_pc equality
on a selected target-table hit. Selecting a table target equal to PC+4
must also produce true; a table-hit or predicted-direction bit alone
is insufficient.

This combinational bit must not depend on imem_data, out.instr, decoded
immediates, flush, redirect, redirect_target, or live resolution inputs.
Like out.pc and out.predicted_next_pc, drive it even when the instruction
output is replaced by a NOP. In ID, copy the bit without arithmetic or
comparison into its single payload register: zero on reset, hold on the
existing backend stall, otherwise capture regardless of flush. Preserve
the full predicted_next_pc and the independent ctrl/valid flush logic.
There is one additional pipeline state bit and no extra pipeline stage.

Factor EX prediction validation by the resolved successor class. For
ordinary instructions, untaken branches, and the existing trap-to-PC+4
path, prediction_correct is the held prediction_matches_seq bit. For a
legal taken branch or JAL, compare the full recorded prediction with
the existing EX branch_target = in.pc + in.imm. For a legal JALR,
compare it with the existing forwarded jalr_sum after clearing bit zero.
Compute these target equalities in EX and select their Boolean results;
do not precompute any direct-target equality or PC+imm addition in ID.
Keep redirect = resolve_valid && !prediction_correct. Leave the current
actual_next_pc computation authoritative for redirect_target and RVFI.

Require Boolean equivalence to the old expression on every advancing
instruction: redirect == resolve_valid &&
(actual_next_pc != in.predicted_next_pc). Preserve exact full-address
comparisons, legal and misaligned target handling, taken transfers to
PC+4, stale predictions on non-controls and completed divides, and
changing JALR destinations. Existing resolve_valid qualification,
redirect priority over instruction stalls, backend holds, forwarding,
memory side effects, retirement order, and nret=1 remain authoritative.

Keep all sixteen predictor rows, PC[5:2] indexing, full tags and targets,
binary saturating counters, command encoding, allocation/invalidation
rules, and capture-at-N/commit-at-N+1 training unchanged. The new bit
describes the same pre-edge prediction captured with the instruction,
even when training commits on its acceptance edge. It must never be
recomputed for a held instruction from newer table contents. No policy,
predictor capacity, benchmark-specific rule, or evaluation change is
part of this hypothesis.

The intended benefit is moving sequential next-PC equality before the
ID/EX boundary and removing the selected actual_next_pc bus from EX's
mismatch comparator. Expect unchanged predictions, recoveries, and
bracketed cycles, with an unmeasured three-percent fitness gain from
higher median Fmax. Confidence is low: the added IF equality may become
critical, separate target comparisons may increase LUT/routing cost,
and unchanged ALU or predictor-maintenance paths may still set Fmax.

Inspect mapped cones to confirm that the new metadata D input has no
combinational recovery/NOP/decode dependency, and that EX uses its
registered value for sequential recovery. Compare the incoming and
candidate designs under identical binaries and ready schedules, retaining
the independent full-next-PC mismatch assertion. Run unchanged lint,
cocotb, formal, stalled cosim, and all three FPGA P&R seeds. Report
marker-bracketed cycles, recoveries, median Fmax, LUT4/FF cost, and the
three critical paths. Compute fitness using unrounded iterations/cycle.
Validate the requested 6 KB, -O3, ten-iteration workload with both bus
stalls, canonical CRCs d4b0/be52/5e47, bounded accesses, both markers,
and the literal Correct operation validated. If existing evaluation
still reproduces the historical score with a 2 KB image, report that
separately from the canonical 6 KB comparison without editing the gates.

implementation_notes:
# Sequential prediction validation from unflushed IF state

Implemented the hypothesis on incoming commit `248468e`. Functional behavior is
unchanged in the comparisons below, but the measured timing benefit did not
materialize: median Fmax and fitness both regress **10.4864798877%**.

## Implementation

- Added exactly one `prediction_matches_seq` field to the combinational IF
  bundle and one bit to the existing ID/EX payload. Its meaning is the full
  equality of the accepted prediction and modulo-2^32 PC+4.
- IF reuses one `seq_pc = pc + 32'd4` expression for sequential prediction and
  the equality. The bit is driven from raw PC and committed lookup state even
  while the instruction output is replaced by a NOP. It has no instruction,
  decode, recovery, or live resolution input.
- ID copies the bit in the existing payload register group: zero on reset,
  hold on backend stall, otherwise capture, including flush. No ID arithmetic,
  comparison, new enable, or additional stage was introduced.
- EX selects Boolean match results. PC+4 successors use the registered bit;
  legal taken branches/JAL compare the full prediction with `branch_target`;
  legal JALR compares with the forwarded `jalr_sum` with bit zero cleared.
  `actual_next_pc`, redirect target, resolve qualification, and RVFI remain
  authoritative and unchanged.
- All 16 predictor rows, PC[5:2] indexing, full tags/targets, counters, commands,
  allocation/invalidation, and capture-at-N/commit-at-N+1 training are unchanged.
  The external contract remains `nret: 1`.

## Verification

- Required Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings or errors.
- Cocotb: all nine original pytest runners PASS; the added comparison runner
  also PASS. The pipeline runner passes all 38 cocotb tests, including the new
  taken-PC+4 branch/JAL/JALR test under zero wait and both bus stalls.
- IF tests check the new bit against independent full equality at every public
  predictor sample, before and after edges. Added selected targets equal to
  PC+4, single-bit target differences at bits 2 through 31, wraparound, and
  unclocked changes to instruction, flush, redirect and resolution inputs.
  Existing pending-commit, alias, counter, stall and reset oracles remain.
- ID tests seed the opposite bit before exercising both values under every
  reset/flush/stall combination, independently of decoding and prediction data.
- Pipeline tests retain the original accepted-prediction mismatch assertion
  and add a separate full-next-PC assertion on every cycle. Accepted metadata,
  backend retention and flush capture are checked independently.
- Incoming/candidate directed comparison: **34 runs, 1,011 cycles, 510
  retirements, 97 recoveries**, with exact equality of original payloads,
  controls, cycle timing, predictions, memory activity and RVFI. Only the new
  metadata field is omitted from cross-design comparison. Programs cover
  changing load-forwarded JALRs, stale ordinary/divide predictions, traps,
  load-use, both bus stalls, pending commits, reset and wrong-path stores.
- Unchanged `tools.eval.cosim`: PASS, selftest plus the evaluator's 2 KB
  CoreMark CRC run. Additional selftest RVFI comparisons against the unchanged
  Python ISS pass with both stalls at seeds 1, 42 and 0x13579bdf (115
  retirements each). Incoming/candidate cycle traces are identical.
- **Local formal: PASS, 53 passed / 0 failed**, using the unchanged
  `bash formal/run_all.sh`, `wrapper_si.sv`, `checks_si.cfg`, and ALTOPS mode.
  No RTL fix attempts or counterexamples. An initial launch exited before
  generating checks because the default Python lacked PyYAML; selecting the
  installed Miniconda Python resolved the environment issue. Actual M-extension
  arithmetic remains covered by the unchanged arithmetic tests and cosim;
  the multiplier/divider RTL was not changed.

## Mapped cones

The candidate's additional state is one `DFFRE`,
`cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_96`, Q = ID/EX bit 166. CE is the existing payload
enable and RESET is the existing reset-only signal.

Backward traversal of its mapped D cone reaches 483 combinational cells and
514 state outputs, exclusively IF PC state and committed predictor state.
This includes the synthesis-generated copies of PC bits used by the target
LUTRAM read address. Asynchronous LUTRAM read addresses were traversed; clocked
write inputs were treated as state boundaries. No decode, instruction-LFSR,
EX, pending-training, flush or redirect state appears in the D cone.

The registered metadata Q reaches the ID/EX valid-reset recovery cone. A
three-valued evaluation of mapped LUTs with an advancing ordinary instruction,
reset low and all unrelated state unknown gives valid.RESET = 1 for metadata
0 and valid.RESET = 0 for metadata 1. Thus sequential recovery uses the held
bit without needing any target comparison to resolve. The IF equality itself
was not the worst critical path in these seeds.

## Workloads and fitness

Both designs used the exact same ELF for each workload, `ITERATIONS=10`,
`COREMARK_OPT=-O3`, and the unchanged harness with `--bench --istall --dstall`
and its default 0xdeadbeef ready-schedule seed. Fitness below is calculated as
`median_Fmax_MHz * 1e6 * (10 / bracketed_cycles)`, without rounding iter/cycle.

| Measurement | Incoming | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Seed 1 Fmax, MHz | 163.83 | 142.29 |
| Seed 2 Fmax, MHz | 155.33 | 150.99 |
| Seed 3 Fmax, MHz | 168.55 | 146.65 |
| Median Fmax, MHz | 163.83 | 146.65 |
| LUT4 | 6,618 | 6,661 |
| FF | 3,198 | 3,199 |
| Requested 6 KB bracketed cycles | 30,822,790 | 30,822,790 |
| 6 KB recoveries inside markers | 550,409 | 550,409 |
| 6 KB recoveries, entire run | 552,348 | 552,348 |
| 6 KB iterations/cycle | 3.2443526364745047e-7 | 3.2443526364745047e-7 |
| 6 KB fitness, iterations/s | 53.15222924336181 | 47.57843141389861 |
| Historical evaluator 2 KB bracketed cycles | 4,215,262 | 4,215,262 |
| 2 KB recoveries inside markers | 80,662 | 80,662 |
| 2 KB recoveries, entire run | 81,398 | 81,398 |
| 2 KB iterations/cycle | 2.372331779139707e-6 | 2.372331779139707e-6 |
| 2 KB fitness, iterations/s | 388.6591153764582 | 347.90245541083806 |

All six P&R runs completed successfully using unmodified `synth.tcl`,
`nextpnr_run.sh` and `tools.eval.fpga`, with the single-retirement wrapper.
The unchanged historical evaluator reports **388.66 -> 347.90** on its 2 KB
image; its displayed `ipc_coremark=2e-6` is rounded and was not used to compute
the numbers above. The requested 6 KB comparison is reported separately.

The 6 KB start/stop cycles are **53,747 / 30,876,537**. Both runs reached EBREAK
after 22,093,920 retirements with `oob:false`, both markers, ten iterations,
`seedcrc=8a02`, `crclist=d4b0`, `crcmatrix=be52`, `crcstate=5e47`,
`crcfinal=5949`, and the literal **Correct operation validated.**

The 2 KB start/stop cycles are **15,229 / 4,230,491**. Both runs reached EBREAK
after 2,937,037 retirements with `oob:false`, both markers, ten iterations,
`seedcrc=e9f5`, `crclist=e714`, `crcmatrix=1fd7`, `crcstate=8e3a`,
`crcfinal=fcaf`, and the validation literal.

Recovery counts were collected by a read-only observer linked to the existing
Verilator model and including the unchanged C++ harness. It also asserts the
independent full-next-PC mismatch on every advancing instruction and checks
the candidate's held sequential bit. Cycle/bus/prediction and RVFI hashes
match between designs for each complete run:

| Workload | Cycle hash (64-bit FNV-1a) | RVFI hash (64-bit FNV-1a) |
|---|---|---|
| 6 KB | 4ea675b489fcb68e | 343eb8fae9f1c7b4 |
| 2 KB | 57769743d7c2834d | f842f18640adf3f8 |

These hashes supplement the exact bounded-program trace comparison; they are
not a formal equivalence proof. A separate observer also checks the exact
requested memory/MMIO bounds, including the narrower `[0x10000000,
0x10000200)` write window, without changing the harness or evaluation gates.
Both workloads pass this stricter check. Their only MMIO write addresses are
0x10000000, 0x10000100 and 0x10000104. The 6 KB run exercises 6,753,957
instruction-not-ready cycles and 6,756,660 data-not-ready cycles.

The existing UART compiler-flags string is hardcoded to `-O2 -march=rv32im`;
the actual build commands used `-O3`. Likewise, `CoreMark Size` prints the
per-algorithm allocation (2000 for total 6000, 666 for total 2000), as defined
in the unchanged `core_main.c`. Neither reporting string was patched.

## Critical paths

The following are final post-route register-to-register paths. The selected
actual-next-PC mismatch path seen in incoming seed 2 no longer limits the
candidate. ALU selection/routing and predictor maintenance remain limiting.

| Design / seed | Source -> destination | Delay ns | Logic / routing ns |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Incoming 1 | ID/EX alu_op[4] -> EX/MEM alu_result[25].D | 6.10 | 2.87 / 3.24 |
| Incoming 2 | ID/EX predicted_next_pc[3] -> ID/EX valid.RESET | 6.44 | 2.77 / 3.67 |
| Incoming 3 | ID/EX alu_op[2] -> EX/MEM alu_result[25].D | 5.93 | 2.78 / 3.15 |
| Candidate 1 | ID/EX alu_op[3] -> EX/MEM alu_result[29].D | 7.03 | 3.52 / 3.51 |
| Candidate 2 | Predictor row 0 tag[1] -> row 0 counter.CE | 6.62 | 2.15 / 4.47 |
| Candidate 3 | ID/EX alu_op[3] -> EX/MEM alu_result[15].D | 6.82 | 3.26 / 3.56 |

Candidate endpoints are respectively `cpu.u_ex.reg_q_DFFR_Q_66.D`,
`cpu.u_if.metadata[0].counter_q_DFFSE_Q_1.CE`, and
`cpu.u_ex.reg_q_DFFR_Q_80.D`. Both candidate ALU paths originate at
`cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_195.Q`; the maintenance path originates at
`cpu.u_if.metadata[0].tag_q_DFFE_Q_24.Q`.

## Deviations, concerns and artifacts

There is no architectural deviation. An additional `test_prediction_compare.py`
replays existing bounded tests for incoming/candidate comparison. Build and
formal artifacts were isolated under `$TMPDIR/seq-validation-r13s2/` to avoid
writing into shared formal, benchmark, tool, or other-core directories. All
candidate RTL/tests match the measured scratch copy; contract files were
checked byte-for-byte against the worktree.

The 6 KB ELF SHA-256 is
`c3b80e911a9292eda01e35bc0034752cb93de46dd68ee8c89cff37bb2bfa7c5c`;
the 2 KB ELF SHA-256 is
`c79d46c4618aeeff26037b744257d1e5c11e0c86acae942bc669e8f110bb7d5a`.
Scratch evidence includes `incoming-directed.json`, `candidate-directed.json`,
`{incoming,candidate}-{2,6}k-measurement.json`, `mapped-cone.json`,
`timing-summary.json`, per-seed `nextpnr.log` files, cocotb XML, and the formal
`candidate/formal/last_run-31875.log` plus per-check PASS statuses.

The hypothesis preserves cycles and recoveries but adds 43 LUT4s and changes
mapping/placement enough to lower Fmax. This is a measured regression, not a

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rewrite only the real multiply candidate inside rtl/alu.sv as one explicit
signed 33-by-33 product, with signedness and low/high selection determined
solely by op[1:0]. Preserve all existing five-bit operation constants.
Their multiply mapping is 11=MUL, 00=MULH, 01=MULHU and 10=MULHSU for
these two low bits. Define fully specified combinational intermediates:

  signed_a = !op[0];
  signed_b = !(op[1] || op[0]);
  a_ext = {signed_a && a[31], a};
  b_ext = {signed_b && b[31], b};
  product = $signed(a_ext) * $signed(b_ext);
  mul_result = (op[1:0] == 2'b11) ? product[31:0] : product[63:32];

Declare a_ext and b_ext as signed 33-bit vectors and product as a signed
66-bit vector, making all expression widths explicit. For MULH both
operands represent signed RV32 values; MULHSU sign-extends only a;
MULHU and MUL zero-extend both. The low 32 bits implement MUL for every
input, and bits 63:32 implement each required high product. Bits 65:64
are intentionally unused. Do not add post-product sign-correction adders.

title: Resolve control flow in MEM from registered forwarded operands
motivation:
Move control-flow execution across the existing EX/MEM register to
separate operand forwarding from branch comparison, JALR target addition,
and recovery. The incoming RTL matches the saved r12 incoming timing
snapshot byte-for-byte: seeds 1 and 3 are limited by ALU selection,
while seed 2 is limited by predicted-next-PC recovery into ID/EX reset.
Related candidates repeatedly expose forwarding through the JALR adder
into predictor target capture. Removing that whole execution dependency
is a more substantial structural experiment than another result mux.

Read LESSONS.md and the structural history. r13s1's parallel result banks
lost 8.34% with wider forwarding/JALR paths; r8s1's registered dependency
matches lost 6.12% when predictor maintenance became limiting. r10s2
delayed predictor training but retained live EX branch execution and
recovery, losing 12.29%. This proposal instead moves the comparator,
full target adders, and architectural recovery to MEM together.

r13s2 records 550,409 recoveries in 30,822,790 canonical 6 KB timed
cycles. One extra cycle per old recovery is a first-order 1.79% cycle
cost, with a break-even clock near 166.76 MHz versus 163.83 MHz.
Training visibility and overlapping stalls can change that estimate.
ALU selection and predictor maintenance remain competing limits, so
a clock improvement is a hypothesis rather than an established result.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition the existing single-issue pipeline: EX computes ordinary
integer/multiply results and captures forwarded operands; MEM performs
all conditional branch comparisons, full-width branch/JAL/JALR target
generation, architectural next-PC selection, and prediction checking.
Use the existing EX/MEM and MEM/WB boundaries. Add no general execution
stage or new instruction buffer. Correctly predicted control flow still
permits one instruction to advance each cycle. A recovery now squashes
the younger instruction in EX as well as the current combinational
IF/ID instruction, costing one additional recovery slot.

Carry the exact accepted predicted_next_pc and decoded immediate into
EX/MEM alongside its existing PC, instruction, controls, and post-forward
rs1_val/rs2_val. Remove the obsolete EX-computed branch_taken,
branch_target, and pc_next fields, replacing their roles explicitly.
MEM computes PC+4 and PC+imm from these registers, and computes JALR as
(registered_rs1 + immediate) with bit zero cleared. Comparisons use the
registered post-forward operands, with the existing signed/unsigned
semantics. Do not add a live forwarding path into MEM resolution.
MEM supplies the resolved pc_next to MEM/WB for RVFI.

Keep JAL/JALR's PC+4 link result available in EX/MEM at its current edge
for ordinary EX/MEM forwarding. A trapping jump must never forward a
link that it will not write, even when its predicted PC already equals
the trap's fall-through PC. Therefore retain only a small unconditional
jump-alignment check in EX: test the low two bits of PC+imm for JAL,
and bit one of the low-two-bit rs1+imm sum for JALR after clearing bit
zero. Include carry from bit zero. Set the existing trap control and
clear reg_write before EX/MEM capture for an illegal-alignment jump.
This must use low-bit arithmetic, not retain a full target adder in EX
or introduce MEM trap feedback through the operand forwarding mux.
A misaligned conditional branch traps only when taken, resolved in MEM;
it has no link write to suppress. Preserve decoder-illegal behavior,
memory-alignment checks, and PC+4 recovery for trapping instructions.

Define resolve_valid from the current EX/MEM instruction's actual MEM
advancement: valid, not reset, and not waiting for its data-bus access.
It must not depend on a younger divide wait, frontend stall, redirect,
or hold_wb output feedback. Generate redirect when this event's complete
architectural next PC differs from its captured prediction. Check every
valid instruction, including ordinary ALU work, loads/stores, completed
divides, and traps, so stale predictor entries recover correctly.
A held memory instruction resolves and trains exactly once when it
advances; no event is generated from an EX/MEM bubble.

Recovery belongs to the older MEM instruction. Let it override younger
load-use and divide interlocks, flush all ID/EX controls and validity,
and insert a complete zero-control/invalid EX/MEM bubble instead of
capturing the younger EX result. Preserve the resolving MEM instruction's
own MEM/WB transfer, accepted memory operation, and eventual retirement.
Route recovery to EX as an explicit squash input and gate divider
request and result consumption with it. A wrong-path divide must not
launch while an older MEM instruction redirects; an older data-memory
hold already blocks launch. Keep accepted divides' eight-edge engine,
saved operands, result retention, and real/ALTOPS schedule unchanged.
The MEM resolve event must remain independent of div_wait, preventing
a wrong-path divide from suppressing its own squash. Clear younger
memory controls before they can enter MEM and drive any bus request.

Preserve the existing backend hold behavior, including MEM/WB forwarding
data retention after its valid bit clears. Keep load-use detection,
EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB forwarding priority, raw RVFI source-value reporting,
x0 behavior, register-file writes, and all ALU arithmetic unchanged.
IF recovery continues to override imem backpressure. The current
ID/EX payload/control split remains: recovery clears controls/valid
without adding recovery to wide payload enables or reset cones.

Feed the existing predictor interface from the MEM resolution event.
Retain all sixteen rows, full tags, PC[5:2] indexing, counters, target
storage, command encoding, private pending events, and committed-state
lookup. Its existing pending capture/commit pipeline is unchanged;
resolution reaches it one execution stage later. Do not train squashed
instructions, replay held instructions, or cancel already accepted
older events on recovery. Reset cancels pending events as before.
Predictor-policy changes and ALU/result-bank redesigns are outside this
single control-flow stage-repartition experiment.

title: Separate predictor fetch tags from row-local training tags
motivation:
The sixteen scalar predictor tags currently serve two different consumers:
their private maintenance comparators and the shared 16-to-1, 26-bit fetch
tag mux. Row-local training and registered events produced the r3s2/r4s1
gains, but the fetch mux still connects those otherwise local registers
across the table. Later experiment reports repeatedly expose tag-to-counter
enable paths. This is a source-level locality opportunity, not a claim that
maintenance is the current winner's worst path: r13s2 reports ALU selection
and prediction recovery as the incoming design's three critical paths.

Predictor associativity, smaller capacity, partial tags, XOR indexing,

implementation_notes:
# Separate predictor fetch tags from row-local training tags

Implemented the proposed storage replication. Correctness and locality checks
pass, but this three-seed trial does **not** meet the fitness acceptance
criterion: median Fmax is 163.35 MHz versus 163.83 MHz incoming, with identical
benchmark cycles. Fitness decreases **0.292986632484904%**. The implementation
is retained for the orchestrator's evaluation.

## Changes and policy preservation

- `cores/bench/rtl/if_stage.sv`: widened the existing sixteen-word target
  array from 30 to 56 bits, storing `{PC[31:6], target[31:2]}`. A single
  asynchronous indexed read supplies both fetch tag equality and the aligned
  target. Removed `tag_view` and the indexed fetch read of scalar row tags.
- Added a 26-bit shared `pending_target_tag_q`, captured with the existing
  target and index under exactly the existing `target_write` qualification.
  The single synchronous write publishes both pending fields on the private
  metadata commit edge. No pending or live-resolution bypass was added.
- Private maintenance RTL is byte-identical to the incoming generate block
  after removing its `tag_view` assignment. Validity, counters, full-tag
  matching, all four commands, saturation, invalidation, and event ordering
  are unchanged. Not-taken and invalidating events never write the RAM.
- Reset still cancels capture and commit, clears all validity, and leaves
  payload storage unreset. Pending validity drains independently of fetch
  stalls, backend holds, and redirects. The new pending tag has no reset.
- Logical table/event storage is 1360/525 bits versus 944/499. Module ports,
  nret=1 retirement, accepted prediction transport, EX recovery, arithmetic,
  scheduling, decoder legality, forwarding, and bus handshakes are unchanged.

## Tests and local formal status

The existing independent integer-counter IF reference, pipeline predictor
oracle, and every existing prediction/timing assertion remain unchanged.

`test_if_stage.py` adds pre-edge and post-edge public-output checks for
continuous same-row aliases differing in every full tag bit, targets differing
in every stored bit, simultaneous capture/commit/fetch, target retention,
matching/nonmatching invalidations, stalls, redirects, idle drain, reset with
a pending write and a simultaneous offered write, and subsequent allocation.

`test_pipeline.py` adds a bounded three-iteration sequence with colliding
branches, changing load-forwarded JALR targets, nine data-memory hold edges,
six instruction-stall edges, three divides, and younger recovery while an
older jump commits. It checks exact public predictions, cycle-positioned
retirement, strict order/PC chaining, unique resolution, targets, links,
operands/results, accepted memory accesses, and absence of wrong-path stores.

An additional allowed test file, `test_prediction_compare.py`, replays directed
tests and optionally compares complete incoming/candidate traces. No trace
fields are omitted or normalized beyond JSON tuple conversion.

Validation results:

- Requested `verilator --lint-only -Wall -Wno-MULTITOP -sv
  +incdir+cores/bench/rtl cores/bench/rtl/*.sv`: **PASS**, no warnings.
- Full cocotb suite: **10 pytest cases passed for each design**, including
  real and ALTOPS arithmetic, five IF tests, and 38 pipeline tests.
- Exact directed comparison: **48 runs, 1,557 cycles, 734 retirements,
  125 recoveries**. All captured pipeline bits, public predictions, cycle
  positions, RVFI fields, and accepted memory transactions agree.
- **Local formal: PASS, 53 passed / 0 failed**, using unchanged
  `bash formal/run_all.sh`, automatic nret=1 selection, `wrapper_si.sv`,
  `checks_si.cfg`, and ALTOPS mode. Passed on the first attempt; no
  counterexamples or RTL fix attempts. Multiplier/divider RTL was unchanged.
- Unchanged `tools.eval.cosim`: **PASS**, selftest plus the evaluator's 2 KB
  CoreMark CRC run, for both designs.
- Additional selftest runs with both bus stalls at seeds 1, 42, and
  0x13579bdf: **115 retirements each**, passing the unchanged Python ISS
  comparison with exact incoming/candidate cycle-positioned trace equality.
- All six FPGA runs completed through the unchanged synthesis script,
  single-retirement benchmark wrapper, `nextpnr_run.sh`, and FPGA evaluator.

## Mapped locality and resource cost

The mapped store is **14 RAM16SDP4 cells**, versus eight incoming. All 56
`fetch_word` bits connect directly to RAM outputs. All 56 write-data bits
connect directly to the shared pending target/tag registers; every cell uses
the same pending write index, write enable, clock, and fetch read address.
There is no scalar `tag_view` net and no second memory lookup port.

All **416 private scalar tag flops** remain. Forward traversal through mapped
combinational cells, stopping at state boundaries, shows that every private
tag bit reaches only its own row's maintenance endpoints. For example, row 0
previously reached 68 nonlocal state ports; the candidate reaches zero. The
same zero-nonlocal-endpoint assertion passes for all sixteen rows.

| Measurement | Incoming | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| nextpnr LUT4 resource use | 6,618 | 6,371 |
| nextpnr FF resource use | 3,198 | 3,260 |
| Explicit mapped flop cells | 3,150 | 3,176 |
| Predictor RAM16SDP4 cells | 8 | 14 |
| Other mapped memory cells, DPX9B | 4 | 4 |

LUT4 use falls 247 (3.7322%). Explicit flop cells increase by the requested
26 pending bits. The nextpnr FF resource metric increases 62; in both designs
that metric exceeds explicit flop cells by six per RAM16SDP4 cell. No extra
RTL pipeline registers, vendor primitives, keep attributes, or synthesis
script changes were introduced.

## Like-for-like benchmarks and fitness

Each workload uses one identical ELF for incoming and candidate, built with
the unchanged benchmark Makefile using `COREMARK_OPT=-O3`, `ITERATIONS=10`,
and total data sizes 2000 or 6000. Both use the unchanged harness with
`--bench --istall --dstall` and default ready-schedule seed 0xdeadbeef.

Fitness is calculated as `(10 / bracketed_cycles) * (median_Fmax_MHz * 1e6)`
using unrounded iterations/cycle. The evaluator's displayed `ipc_coremark`
is rounded and is not used in these calculations.

| Measurement | Incoming | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Seed 1 Fmax, MHz | 163.83 | 166.81 |

| 2 KB fitness, iterations/s | 388.6591153764582 | 387.52039612247115 |
| Requested 6 KB bracketed cycles | 30,822,790 | 30,822,790 |
| 6 KB recoveries inside markers | 550,409 | 550,409 |
| 6 KB recoveries, whole run | 552,348 | 552,348 |
| 6 KB iterations/cycle | 3.2443526364745047e-7 | 3.2443526364745047e-7 |
| 6 KB fitness, iterations/s | 53.15222924336181 | 52.99650031681103 |

The unchanged historical evaluator reproduces **388.66 -> 387.52** for its
2 KB workload. The requested canonical 6 KB result is reported separately.

The 6 KB accepted start/stop markers are at cycles **53,747 / 30,876,537**.
Both designs reach EBREAK after **22,093,920 retirements**, with `oob:false`,
ten iterations, `seedcrc=8a02`, `crclist=d4b0`, `crcmatrix=be52`,

Both runs contain 6,753,957 instruction-not-ready cycles and
6,756,660 data-not-ready cycles.

The 2 KB accepted start/stop markers are at cycles **15,229 / 4,230,491**.
Both designs reach EBREAK after **2,937,037 retirements**, with `oob:false`,

`crcstate=8e3a`, `crcfinal=fcaf`, and the same validation literal.

A read-only observer compiled from stdin and linked to each existing
Verilator model includes the unchanged C++ harness. It checks committed
prediction before/after every edge, exact accepted prediction through EX,
unique issue/resolution/retirement, RVFI order and PC chaining, and the

|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 2 KB | 547,101 / 141,669 | 9936ace0ad8fc67a | 513e265fa104f6c4 | 8936b48ec7b30cd2 |

Hashes use 64-bit FNV-1a and supplement the exact bounded trace comparison;
they are not a formal equivalence proof. The observer adds the narrow
`[0x10000000, 0x10000200)` MMIO bound without modifying the harness's bounds
checks. Its initial link needed the same weak-symbol flags used by the
unchanged Verilator build; this was a validation-environment fix only.

The existing UART compiler-flags string is hardcoded to `-O2 -march=rv32im`;
the actual retained build logs show `-O3`. `CoreMark Size` prints the
per-algorithm allocation, 2000 for the requested total 6000 and 666 for total
2000. These contract-side reporting strings were not edited.

## Routed critical paths

Final post-route register-to-register paths:

| Design / seed | Source -> destination | Delay ns | Logic / routing ns |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Incoming 1 | ID/EX alu_op[4] -> EX/MEM alu_result[25].D | 6.10 | 2.87 / 3.24 |
| Incoming 2 | ID/EX predicted_next_pc[3] -> ID/EX valid.RESET | 6.44 | 2.77 / 3.67 |
| Incoming 3 | ID/EX alu_op[2] -> EX/MEM alu_result[25].D | 5.93 | 2.78 / 3.15 |
| Candidate 1 | Predictor row 12 valid -> row 12 counter[0].CE | 5.99 | 2.39 / 3.61 |
| Candidate 2 | ID/EX alu_op[3] -> EX/MEM alu_result[0].D | 6.20 | 3.77 / 2.43 |
| Candidate 3 | ID/EX predicted_next_pc[18] -> ID/EX valid.RESET | 6.12 | 2.77 / 3.36 |

Candidate endpoints are respectively
`cpu.u_if.metadata[12].counter_q_DFFSE_Q_1.CE`,
`cpu.u_ex.reg_q_DFFR_Q_95.D`, and
`cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_192.RESET`. Their sources are
`cpu.u_if.metadata[12].valid_q_DFFRE_Q.Q`,
`cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_194.Q`, and `cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_77.Q`.
The fetch tag mux is removed, but local maintenance, ALU selection, and
prediction recovery still limit these placements. Lower LUT use therefore
does not establish the proposed clock improvement.

## Deviations, concerns, and retained evidence

There is no architectural deviation. The extra trace-comparison test is
within the allowed test surface. Checks ran in isolated scratch copies under
`$TMPDIR/fetch-tags-r14s2/` to avoid generated writes into shared formal,
benchmark, tool, or other-core directories. All measured candidate RTL/tests
match the worktree. A byte comparison verified 479 copied contract/reference
files against their originals.

The requested implementation notes are in the current worktree directory.
All source changes are confined to bench RTL and `test_*.py` files.

Retained evidence includes `formal.log`, both test/cosim/FPGA evaluation logs,
the formal per-check PASS statuses, `incoming-directed.json`,
`candidate-directed.json`, `stalled-selftest.json`, `mapped-locality.json`,
`timing-summary.json`, `fitness-summary.json` with full-precision decimal
fitness, all six `nextpnr.log`/mapped/routed JSON artifacts,
both benchmark build logs, and `{incoming,candidate}-{2,6}k-measurement.json`.

The measured 2 KB ELF SHA-256 is
`dcdb665667da1c6a868857c96a9eda17af9dcd779a6445d457f34a074d7ebf59`.
The measured 6 KB ELF SHA-256 is
`30ef880019ab96effb260b04eb234a610b3447e4e7d2973c0f331eb34b1b59e2`.

The intended locality is confirmed, with unchanged execution behavior on the
tested schedules. Added RAM resources and changed mapping/placement did not
produce a higher median clock/cycle product in this trial. No policy changes
or evaluation changes were made to improve the reported result.

title: Share one bidirectional barrel shifter across SLL, SRL and SRA
motivation:
The winner's saved incoming RTL in .tmp/seq-validation-r13s2/incoming/
matches every current bench RTL file. Its routed seeds are 163.83,
155.33 and 168.55 MHz; two are limited by ALU operation control through
result selection into EX/MEM, while the other is limited by prediction
recovery. The incoming synthesis log in .tmp/mul-factor-r14s0/ reports
no resource-sharing candidates for the ALU's separate SLL, SRL and SRA
operators. Later Boolean optimization can share some gates, so this
does not establish three wholly independent mapped barrel shifters.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the three combinational shift expressions in rtl/alu.sv
with one bidirectional barrel shifter built around a signed 33-bit
arithmetic right shift. Reverse the 32 operand bits before and after
that common shifter for SLL. Reversal itself is fixed wiring; selecting
reversed versus original order requires muxes and must be costed.

Keep all current five-bit ALU operation constants. They encode SLL=7,
SRL=8 and SRA=9. Inside the speculative shift candidate, derive:
  shift_left = !op[3];
  sign_fill = op[3] && op[0] && a[31];
  reversed_a[i] = a[31-i], for i from 0 through 31;
  shift_operand = shift_left ? reversed_a : a;
  signed_operand = {sign_fill, shift_operand};
  shifted = $signed(signed_operand) >>> b[4:0];
  reversed_shifted[i] = shifted[31-i], for i from 0 through 31;
  shift_result = shift_left ? reversed_shifted : shifted[31:0];
Declare signed_operand and shifted as signed 33-bit vectors and the
other data vectors as 32 bits. The unused shifted[32] is intentional.
Use constant-index generate wiring for reversal, with no variable
reversal loop, second variable shifter, or synthesis-only behavior.

Combine ALU_SLL, ALU_SRL and ALU_SRA into one exact-opcode case arm
returning shift_result. This full-opcode arm is the only admission
gate for the candidate. Its internal direction and sign controls use
only the stated opcode bits; non-shift opcodes may compute arbitrary
but fully defined speculative shift values that are never selected.
Introduce no X values, don't-cares, new operation codes or extra
full-family qualification on the shifter inputs. Retain b[4:0]
masking, including when b has nonzero upper bits.

Preserve every non-shift ALU arm and the default-zero case verbatim,
including the multiplier expressions, individual ALTOPS substitutions
and divider result selection. Both real and ALTOPS builds use this
same integer shifter. Keep the existing combinational latency, ports,
pipeline registers, forwarding, raw RVFI operands, hazard equations,
predictor policy and event timing, and eight-edge divider handshake.
This is one datapath-sharing experiment, with no pipeline redesign.

The intended benefit is a smaller shift network and one shift-family
contribution to the ALU result mux instead of three. This may reduce
routing pressure and selection delay, improving Fmax at identical IPC.
Estimate an unmeasured two-percent fitness gain with low confidence.
Added input/output direction muxes can create a slower operand or
opcode path; existing gate sharing can make the area saving small;
recovery, JALR or predictor maintenance can still dominate timing.
Inspect the synthesized common shifter and final selection cone,
report LUT4/FF counts, confirm the existing single MULT36X36 remains,
and compare all three routed critical paths. Area savings alone do
not validate the hypothesis; reject it if median fitness regresses.

Run the unchanged lint, cocotb, formal and stalled ISS cosim gates.
Compare identical binaries and bus-ready schedules against the
incoming winner, requiring identical valid RVFI records and their
cycle positions, accepted memory transactions, predictions and
marker-bracketed cycles. Evaluate the requested 6 KB, -O3,
ITERATIONS=10 workload with both bus stalls, bounded accesses,
start/stop markers, canonical CRCs d4b0/be52/5e47 and the literal
Correct operation validated. Keep historical 2 KB score comparisons
separately labelled. Calculate fitness using full-precision
iterations/bracketed-cycles times median Fmax_Hz, not rounded IPC.
Preserve nret=1, top-level IO, trap/decoder discipline, retirement
order and every invariant; do not modify any protected evaluator.

title: Execute multiply-high in an eight-edge engine sharing one 16x16 multiplier
motivation:
Remove high-product execution and signedness selection from the fast
execution resource without delaying ordinary MUL. The incoming design
computes three full products combinationally and lets synthesis share
their signedness and low/high selection. Saved incoming routed reports
show ALU-operation-to-EX/MEM-result paths limiting seeds 1 and 3; recovery
limits seed 2. This motivates a resource and scheduling change, although
it does not establish multiplication itself as the critical arithmetic.

LESSONS.md and the structural experiment history argue against merely
moving the same arithmetic across a register. r9s1 moved high products
into MEM, created a second MULT36X36, and lost 18.10% fitness. r11s1
moved all multiplies into MEM and added timed MUL dependency bubbles;
r13s1 widened forwarding with parallel result banks and lost 8.34%.
Instead, replace the high-product resource with one small, sequentially
reused multiplier and retain the existing single EX/MEM result register.
r9s1 and r11s1 measured zero high multiplies in both timed CoreMark
configurations, versus 1,269,000 ordinary MULs in the canonical 6 KB
bracket. Extra high-operation latency should therefore have little
direct benchmark cost; initialization and random-stall phase still need
measurement. r14s1's liveness failure requires respecting the existing
eight-edge long-operation budget and retaining EX-stage recovery.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep RV32I operations and MUL combinational in EX. Execute MULH, MULHU,
and MULHSU in a blocking eight-edge unit using four successive unsigned
16x16 partial products from one shared multiplication operator. Remove
the combinational signed/signed, signed/unsigned, and unsigned-high
products from the production fast ALU. Its real MUL path computes only
the unsigned low 32 bits, with no operation-dependent multiplier sign
inputs or high-half selection. Preserve operation encodings and decoder
legality. This is one structural resource split, not a change to the
common instruction pipeline depth, predictor, or forwarding topology.

Add mulh_unit.sv with request-ready and retained result-valid/result-ready
handshakes. Capture both post-forward 32-bit operands and the operation
on the accepting edge; subsequent computation uses only captured state.
Use one behavioral 16x16 unsigned multiplication expression with muxed
registered operand halves. Do not describe four parallel multipliers or
rely on synthesis to serialize them. Let A0/B0 be the low halves and
A1/B1 the high halves of the unsigned operand bit patterns. Use this
fixed schedule, counting acceptance as edge 1:

  Edge 1: capture operands, operation, and signed-correction flags.
  Edge 2: capture the upper 16 bits of P00 = A0*B0.
  Edge 3: capture P01 = A0*B1 into a 33-bit cross-term accumulator.
  Edge 4: add P00[31:16] to that accumulator; capture P10 = A1*B0.
  Edge 5: add zero-extended P10 to the accumulator; capture P11 = A1*B1.
  Edge 6: capture H = P11 + accumulator[32:16].
  Edge 7: capture H minus B when A is interpreted signed and A[31]=1.
  Edge 8: capture the result minus A when B is interpreted signed and
          B[31]=1; assert result_valid.

Preserve the 33rd cross-term bit and perform the final high-word
additions/subtractions modulo 2^32. A is signed for MULH/MULHSU; B is
signed only for MULH. Thus MULHU returns high_unsigned(A*B), MULHSU
subtracts sign(A)*B, and MULH additionally subtracts sign(B)*A.
Include carry-heavy and negative boundary cases in independent tests.
Organize the accumulator/correction phases around one shared 33-bit
add/subtract datapath where practical; do not put an addition after
the partial-product multiplier in the same capture cone. This schedule
separates product capture, cross-term carry, and signed correction.

Generalize the ALU/EX long-operation handshake to dispatch an accepted
request to either the unchanged div_unit or the new high unit, according
to the legal opcode. Only the selected unit receives req_valid or
result_ready. Select its ready/valid/result consistently. A request is
ready only when the execution resource is unoccupied; a retained result
prevents relaunch, including on its consumption edge. Illegal, invalid,
reset, and older-memory-held instructions cannot launch either unit.
Keep ordinary MUL independent of this request interface.

EX retains the instruction and saves both actually accepted forwarded
operands for RVFI, just as the divider currently does. Generalize the
existing divide wait to hold fetch and ID/EX while older instructions
drain exactly once and complete zero-control EX/MEM bubbles are inserted.
Actual dmem holds retain their existing priority and MEM/WB forwarding
payload. Once the high result is valid, consume it into the same scalar
EX/MEM.alu_result on edge 9; MEM/WB receives it on edge 10. No extra
forwarding source or late-result load-use interlock is introduced.
A following dependent instruction uses normal EX/MEM forwarding, and
high operations with rd=x0 still execute and retire exactly once.

Keep EX prediction checking and training suppressed during the wait
and emit them once on advancement, using the exact accepted prediction.
This includes stale predictions attached to a high multiply. Preserve
redirect priority over imem stalls, all memory-side effects, and source
snapshots after older WB data drains. Reset cancels requests, computation,
and retained results. Consecutive long operations must not consume each
other's operands or results. Retain the divider's existing eight-edge
real and ALTOPS behavior without adding a dispatch or completion edge.
With ready buses, a high multiply following a cold redirect must meet
the same ten-cycle retirement-gap bound already met by division; prove
this with the unchanged liveness check before FPGA evaluation.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, latch the existing high-operation formulas
from accepted operands and publish them on the identical eighth edge:
MULH=(A+B)^0xf6583fb7, MULHU=(A+B)^0x949ce5e8,
MULHSU=(A-B)^0xecfbe137. Keep MUL=(A+B)^0x5876063e combinational and
leave all DIV/REM substitutions unchanged. Do not retain a fast high
result for formal or simulation. Adapt every existing high-operation
arithmetic test to its handshake, retaining its independent expected
values and adding CPU retirement coverage rather than deleting vectors.

Predict an unmeasured 4% fitness improvement with low confidence. The
intended gain is a simpler fast multiplier/result cone at essentially
unchanged timed cycles. The new unit adds state and a small multiplier;
its phase muxes, carry datapath, EX wait control, unchanged predictor
maintenance, or JALR/recovery routing may erase that benefit. Confirm
in the synthesized netlist that the high unit uses one 16x16 operator,
has no full-width multiplier, and starts its product cones at captured
operands. Inspect actual DSP usage and all three routed critical paths;
source-level separation alone is not evidence of improved timing.

Run unchanged lint, cocotb, formal including liveness, stalled ISS cosim,
and three-seed FPGA gates. Compare identical incoming/candidate ELFs
using exact iterations/marker-bracketed-cycles times median Fmax in Hz.
Recount timed high operations and measure any stall-phase cycle change.
Validate the canonical 6 KB, ten-iteration, -O3 run with both random bus
stalls, accepted start/stop markers, bounded accesses, d4b0/be52/5e47
CRCs, and Correct operation validated. The experiment log associates
388.66 with the protected evaluator's 2 KB workload; report that
like-for-like comparison separately from the requested 6 KB result.
Preserve nret=1, module core's ports, exact channel-0 retirement order,
decoder/trap checks, all existing correctness assertions, and every
protected file. All implementation changes are confined to cores/bench.

implementation_notes:
Implemented the eight-edge multiply-high resource split. Correctness and
liveness gates pass, but the predicted low-confidence 4% fitness improvement
was not observed: measured fitness regresses 13.7398523% on both workloads.
Median routed Fmax falls from 163.83 to 141.32 MHz with unchanged timed cycles.

`cores/bench/rtl/mulh_unit.sv` captures operands and the accepted operation's
signed-correction flags, then reuses one unsigned 16x16 multiplication
expression. Acceptance is edge 1; edges 2–5 capture P00[31:16], P01, P10,
and P11, with the scheduled cross-term additions on edges 4 and 5. Edge 6
captures unsigned H, edge 7 subtracts B when required, and edge 8 subtracts
A when required and asserts retained result-valid. Cross terms retain bit
32; high-word arithmetic wraps modulo 2^32. The correction flags encode the
operation's arithmetic effect, avoiding an otherwise unused opcode register.
ALTOPS captures the specified formula on acceptance and publishes it only
on the identical eighth edge.

`alu.sv` now computes only unsigned MUL-low combinationally. Its generalized
long-operation interface dispatches directly to the unchanged divider or
the high unit. Two ownership bits retain occupancy and engine selection
through result consumption, so live input changes cannot switch engines,
and a retained result prevents relaunch on its consumption edge. Only the
selected unit receives request-valid or result-ready. Ordinary MUL remains
independent of the interface.

`ex_stage.sv`, `hazard_unit.sv`, and `core.sv` generalize the existing divide
interlock to all seven long operations. Accepted forwarded operands are
saved for RVFI; ID/EX holds the exact prediction and instruction metadata.
Older work drains through complete zero-control EX/MEM bubbles. Actual
memory holds retain priority and preserve MEM/WB forwarding data. Results
enter the existing scalar EX/MEM result register on edge 9 and MEM/WB on
edge 10. Prediction resolution and training occur once on advancement.
Decoder encodings, legality, divider arithmetic/controller, forwarding
sources, predictor maintenance, core ports, nret=1, and RVFI order logic
are unchanged. No extra execution or completion stage was added.

title: Taken-only tagged target prediction without direction counters
motivation:
The current sixteen-entry predictor combines a valid full-tag target hit
with a two-bit direction counter. Its row-local maintenance therefore
needs full-tag qualification, hit-versus-allocation selection, counter
saturation, and conditional counter writes. The r14s2 experiment isolated
fetch tags but still encountered a 5.99 ns valid-to-counter-enable path
in one routed seed, with essentially unchanged overall fitness. Earlier
thermometer counters (r6s0), another tag-validation stage (r6s1), and
untagged bimodal counters (r8s2) all regressed. None removed the direction
counters entirely while keeping full-tag-qualified target residency.

This motivates a simpler prediction policy rather than another encoding
of the same counter. The saved incoming r14s2 measurements reproduce
550,409 recoveries in 30,822,790 bracketed cycles for canonical 6 KB
CoreMark. Recovery bubbles are relatively infrequent, so accepting some
extra misses may pay if removing counter logic improves routed frequency.
This is not evidence that counter maintenance is the current winner's
worst path: its saved three seeds instead expose ALU selection and
prediction recovery. The proposed timing gain remains unmeasured.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the existing tagged two-bit hysteresis policy with a taken-only
target table. Keep sixteen direct-mapped rows, index PC[5:2], full
PC[31:6] tags, full aligned target[31:2] payloads, and the existing
private resolution-event pipeline. A valid matching entry always predicts
its stored target; a miss predicts PC+4. Remove both counter bits per
row, counter_view, counter_d, counter saturation, and the indexed counter
selection from fetch. The existing valid bit now also represents whether
the resident PC's last committed control outcome was taken.

Apply these exact rules to each registered pending event at the existing
commit edge, using the row's current tag and validity:
  JUMP: set valid and write the event tag and aligned resolved target.
  TAKEN: perform exactly the same allocation or refresh as JUMP.
  NOT_TAKEN: clear valid only on a valid full-tag match; otherwise do nothing.
  INVALIDATE: clear valid only on a valid full-tag match; otherwise do nothing.
NOT_TAKEN and INVALIDATE retain the stored tag and target payloads, which
become inert when validity clears. In particular, a not-taken branch at
an alias PC must not evict another PC's entry or train shared direction
state. Legal jumps and taken branches always allocate, regardless of the
previous row contents. Trapping resolutions never allocate. No counter,
auxiliary history, return stack, capacity change, hash, instruction
predecode, or extra prediction source is part of this hypothesis.

Preserve classified event capture at edge N and commit at N+1. Retain
private pending tags and the aligned indexed target-write transaction;
commit metadata and target together. Accept the next event while applying
the previous event against current row state, including consecutive
same-row aliases. Pending validity drains independently of fetch stalls,
backend holds, and redirects. Reset clears table validity and cancels
pending events and target writes with priority over capture and commit.
Lookup uses committed state only; fetch on a commit edge selects the
pre-edge prediction, without pending-event or live-EX bypass.

Preserve the existing classified row-event capture boundary rather than
replacing it with raw resolution-field capture. The r8s2 notes show that
synthesis changed the winner's one-hot pending commands to binary and
exposed a long EX-to-command path. Inspect the new mapped capture cones
and command encoding as well as the removed counter cones; a similar
capture-path regression would falsify the timing premise. Any encoding
adjustment must serve this same event boundary, without new pipeline
